TW-KEE.name: Keelung
TW-KEE.intro: A rainy harbor city once known as the “gateway to Taiwan.” Forts from the Sino-French War and the story of the port's construction live on in its gun batteries and colorful waterfront.
TW-KEE.rinka: I want to eat my way from one end of Keelung's Miaokou Night Market to the other! And the harbor lights at night? So romantic.

TW-TPE.name: Taipei
TW-TPE.intro: Taiwan's capital. River-port trade made Monga (Bangka) and Dadaocheng rich in the Qing era, and under Japanese rule the city became the seat of government. Today it's a city of culture, home to the National Palace Museum and Taipei 101.
TW-TPE.rinka: Taipei is my home turf! The night view from 101, the treasures at the Palace Museum, the fried chicken at Shilin Night Market... you can't skip any of them.

TW-NWT.name: New Taipei
TW-NWT.intro: Taiwan's largest city, wrapped around Taipei. Gold mines in Jiufen, coal mines in Pingxi, an old treaty port in Tamsui: its industrial past has become its top sights.
TW-NWT.rinka: The moment the lanterns light up in Jiufen, it's so pretty I get goosebumps. And you have to send up a sky lantern in Pingxi!

TW-TAO.name: Taoyuan
TW-TAO.intro: Taiwan's gateway by air. Daxi's woodcraft and old street recall the days of river trade, while Shimen Reservoir tells the modern chapter.
TW-TAO.rinka: Don't rush straight off from the airport! Dried tofu on Daxi Old Street and the lake views at Shimen Reservoir are worth the detour.

TW-HSZ.name: Hsinchu City
TW-HSZ.intro: Northern Taiwan's oldest walled town, once called Zhuqian. Qing-era gates and temples, Japanese-era buildings and a modern science park all share the same streets.
TW-HSZ.rinka: Hsinchu rice noodles and meatball soup are a match made in heaven! A stroll around the old East Gate feels great, too.

TW-HSQ.name: Hsinchu County
TW-HSQ.intro: A mountain county of Hakka and Atayal communities. Hakka villages in Beipu and Neiwan await, along with the giant-tree forest of Smangus.
TW-HSQ.rinka: Ride the little Neiwan Line train slowly into the mountains, with nothing but green out the window. And try Hakka lei cha, the pounded tea!

TW-ILA.name: Yilan
TW-ILA.intro: A land of hot springs and water on the Lanyang Plain. Once home to the Kavalan people, it's now a classic weekend escape, linked straight to Taipei by the Hsuehshan Tunnel.
TW-ILA.rinka: In Yilan, hot springs and scallion pancakes are your reward on a rainy day. I also recommend whale watching off Guishan Island!

TW-MIA.name: Miaoli
TW-MIA.intro: A mountainous Hakka county, known for the railway heritage of the old Mountain Line, the ruined Longteng Bridge and winter strawberry picking in Dahu.
TW-MIA.rinka: Longteng Bridge's red brick looks its best at sunset. Come in May and tung blossoms cover the whole mountainside.

TW-TXG.name: Taichung
TW-TXG.intro: Central Taiwan's hub city, with sights ranging from the teahouse where bubble tea was born to sunsets over Gaomei Wetlands and the mountain resort of Wuling.
TW-TXG.rinka: Taichung is where bubble tea was born! Rainbow Village, the National Taichung Theater... one day isn't enough to photograph it all.

TW-CHA.name: Changhua
TW-CHA.intro: Home to Lukang, the “second” town in the old saying “First Tainan, second Lukang, third Monga.” A center of temple architecture and crafts, surrounded by plains of flower farms and oyster beds.
TW-CHA.rinka: Lukang's alleys are packed with old stories. And the view from the Great Buddha on Baguashan is the best!

TW-NAN.name: Nantou
TW-NAN.intro: Taiwan's only landlocked county. Thao legends at Sun Moon Lake, the misty forests of Xitou and the aroma of Dongding oolong: this is the island's inland heart.
TW-NAN.rinka: Sun Moon Lake in the morning is like a mirror. Cycling all the way around it is my number-one route in Taiwan!

TW-YUN.name: Yunlin
TW-YUN.intro: Taiwan's farming heartland. It's a center of Mazu worship at Beigang Chaotian Temple, the birthplace of budaixi glove puppetry and the home of Gukeng coffee.
TW-YUN.rinka: The buzz at Beigang Chaotian Temple and all that rooftop decoration are breathtaking. And the smell of Gukeng coffee? I can't resist it.

TW-CYI.name: Chiayi City
TW-CYI.intro: A city that grew rich on Alishan's timber. Japanese-era cypress houses still stand, along with the baseball legend made famous by the film KANO.
TW-CYI.rinka: I always end up eating two bowls of Chiayi turkey rice! Wandering the Japanese houses at Hinoki Village is fun, too.

TW-CYQ.name: Chiayi County
TW-CYQ.intro: From coastal wetlands to the sea of clouds on Alishan, it rises 3,000 m. Tsou valleys, Fenqihu lunch boxes and high-mountain tea gardens: “vertical Taiwan” in a single county.
TW-CYQ.rinka: Sunrise and the sea of clouds on Alishan are worth however long you wait. The mountain train through the forest will blow you away!

TW-TNN.name: Tainan
TW-TNN.intro: Taiwan's oldest city. Four hundred years of history, from the Dutch to Koxinga to the Qing, lie layer upon layer in this old capital. It's also Taiwan's street-food capital, the home of xiaochi, or small eats.
TW-TNN.rinka: Tainan is food heaven! Beef soup for breakfast, then sunset in Anping. That's a perfect day.

TW-KHH.name: Kaohsiung
TW-KHH.intro: The south's largest port city. It grew from a treaty port into an international trade hub, and today its art districts sit side by side with old harbor-town charm.
TW-KHH.rinka: Kaohsiung: sunset over the harbor, an art walk around Pier-2, then Ruifeng Night Market. Perfect!

TW-PIF.name: Pingtung
TW-PIF.intro: Taiwan's southern tip. The mountains of the Paiwan and Rukai peoples, bluefin tuna in Donggang and the coral reefs of Kenting: this is tropical Taiwan.
TW-PIF.rinka: The sea at Kenting is unbelievably blue! Play in the waves at Baisha Bay and your worries just wash away.

TW-HUA.name: Hualien
TW-HUA.intro: The gateway to eastern Taiwan, squeezed between the Central Mountain Range and the Pacific. Its pride: marble gorges and Amis culture.
TW-HUA.rinka: Taroko Gorge is so huge it leaves you speechless. I could listen to the waves at Qixingtan all day.

TW-TTT.name: Taitung
TW-TTT.intro: A slow-paced land once called “behind the mountains.” Prehistoric sites, Indigenous songs and skies full of hot-air balloons await.
TW-TTT.rinka: You have to see the Taitung hot-air balloon festival at least once! Cycling the rice-field roads of Chishang feels amazing, too.

TW-PEN.name: Penghu
TW-PEN.intro: A basalt archipelago and the first place in Taiwan settled by Han Chinese. Stone fish weirs and old stone houses tell the story of life by the sea.
TW-PEN.rinka: Penghu's heart-shaped stone weir is best at low tide! The summer fireworks festival is so fun you'll want to move there.

TW-KIN.name: Kinmen
TW-KIN.intro: An island that was once the front line. Southern Fujian (Minnan) villages, Western-style mansions built by emigrants back from Southeast Asia and wartime tunnels stand side by side, and the air smells of sorghum liquor.
TW-KIN.rinka: Kinmen's old Minnan houses and Wind Lion God statues are so full of character. Gongtang peanut candy and kitchen knives are the classic souvenirs.

TW-LIE.name: Matsu
TW-LIE.intro: An archipelago where the stone houses of Eastern Min culture still stand. Once a military front line, now a seaside destination famous for its glowing “blue tears.”
TW-LIE.rinka: Matsu's blue tears look like the starry sky fell into the sea. The wartime tunnels and the local laojiu rice wine come with plenty of stories, too.

TW-KEE|和平島地質公園.name: Heping Island Geopark
TW-KEE|和平島地質公園.text: Sea erosion has carved this coastal park into “tofu rocks,” mushroom rocks and other strange shapes. Relics from the Dutch period remain too, so nature and history meet here.

TW-KEE|正濱漁港色彩屋.name: Zhengbin Fishing Port Colorful Houses
TW-KEE|正濱漁港色彩屋.text: Rows of brightly painted houses reflected in the harbor have earned it the nickname “Taiwan's Cinque Terre.” A photo hotspot with a past: under Japanese rule, this was Taiwan's busiest port.

TW-KEE|國立海洋科技博物館.name: National Museum of Marine Science and Technology
TW-KEE|國立海洋科技博物館.text: A large museum all about ocean science and technology. The exhibits are extensive and suit all ages, so it's a good bet in rainy Keelung.

TW-KEE|情人湖濱海大道.name: Lover's Lake Coastal Road
TW-KEE|情人湖濱海大道.text: A coastal road of about 5 km squeezed between the mountains and the sea. It follows Keelung's longest stretch of natural shoreline, with reefs and surf all the way.

TW-KEE|白米甕砲台(荷蘭城).name: Baimiweng Fort (Dutch Fort)
TW-KEE|白米甕砲台(荷蘭城).text: An old battery with four gun emplacements on a hill overlooking Keelung Harbor. Come for the view out to where the sea meets the sky.

TW-KEE|必應創造展演空間.name: B'IN LIVE SPACE Keelung
TW-KEE|必應創造展演空間.text: A live music and culture venue that opened in 2024 in a renovated former bus terminal. A new landmark where a historic building meets music.

TW-KEE|潮境智能海洋館.name: Chaojing Smart Ocean Hall
TW-KEE|潮境智能海洋館.text: Taiwan's first “ocean meets tech” aquarium, where AR, VR and immersive projections let you experience the sea.

TW-KEE|陽明海洋文化藝術館.name: Yang Ming Oceanic Culture and Art Museum
TW-KEE|陽明海洋文化藝術館.text: Housed in the former Keelung branch office of the NYK shipping line, built in 1915, the museum tells the story of Keelung Harbor and the island's maritime culture.

TW-KEE|拉波波村.name: Lapopo Village Campground
TW-KEE|拉波波村.text: A glamping site inspired by the villages of southern France, tucked between a mountain stream and the forest.

TW-KEE|暖東舊道 (淡蘭古道TK2-3).name: Nuandong Old Trail (Tamsui–Kavalan Trails)
TW-KEE|暖東舊道 (淡蘭古道TK2-3).text: A section of the 200-year-old Tamsui–Kavalan Trails. Mountain paths once used to haul tea and camphor are now quiet hiking routes.

TW-TPE|台北101.name: Taipei 101
TW-TPE|台北101.text: Taipei's bamboo-inspired landmark and a former world's tallest building. The observatory on the 89th floor looks out over the whole Taipei Basin.

TW-TPE|國立故宮博物院.name: National Palace Museum
TW-TPE|國立故宮博物院.text: Home to some 700,000 treasures from the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, spanning five thousand years of Chinese civilization. It's often ranked among the world's four great museums.

TW-TPE|國立中正紀念堂.name: National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
TW-TPE|國立中正紀念堂.text: A stately memorial hall of blue tiles and white walls. Don't miss the vast plaza, the grand archway and the changing of the guard.

TW-TPE|艋舺龍山寺.name: Bangka Lungshan Temple
TW-TPE|艋舺龍山寺.text: Founded about 300 years ago, it's one of Taipei's oldest temples. Famous for its intricate carvings and steady stream of worshippers, it's the spiritual heart of Wanhua.

TW-TPE|陽明山國家公園_冷水坑.name: Yangmingshan National Park: Lengshuikeng
TW-TPE|陽明山國家公園_冷水坑.text: A volcanic valley at the foot of Mt. Qixing with hot springs, a milky pond and nature trails. A Yangmingshan classic.

TW-TPE|新北投溫泉商圈.name: Xinbeitou Hot Spring Area
TW-TPE|新北投溫泉商圈.text: Taipei's hot-spring retreat, popular since the Japanese era. Milky-white waters, Thermal Valley and the Hot Spring Museum are all within walking distance.

TW-TPE|大稻埕辜宅.name: Koo Family Salt House, Dadaocheng
TW-TPE|大稻埕辜宅.text: A riverside Western-style mansion built in 1910 by a wealthy salt merchant. The “Salt House” still captures Dadaocheng's days as a trading hub.

TW-TPE|西門紅樓.name: The Red House, Ximending
TW-TPE|西門紅樓.text: An octagonal red-brick hall built in 1908. Taiwan's first public market is now a hub for arts and culture.

TW-TPE|南港山系_象山親山步道.name: Elephant Mountain Trail
TW-TPE|南港山系_象山親山步道.text: A popular hike famous for its head-on view of Taipei 101. Time it for dusk and stay for the city lights.

TW-TPE|士林官邸_士林官邸公園.name: Shilin Official Residence Park
TW-TPE|士林官邸_士林官邸公園.text: The former residence and gardens of Chiang Kai-shek and his wife. With a rose garden and flowers in every season, it's a graceful oasis in the city.

TW-NWT|九份老街.name: Jiufen Old Street
TW-NWT|九份老街.text: A hillside town built on gold mining. Red lanterns, stone steps and teahouses looking out to sea make it one of Taiwan's most evocative sights.

TW-NWT|野柳地質公園.name: Yehliu Geopark
TW-NWT|野柳地質公園.text: A cape of strange rock formations, famous for the Queen's Head. Sea-carved landscapes like these are rare anywhere in the world.

TW-NWT|十分瀑布公園.name: Shifen Waterfall Park
TW-NWT|十分瀑布公園.text: A curtain-shaped waterfall nicknamed “Taiwan's Niagara.” The roar of the falling water is spectacular.

TW-NWT|新平溪煤礦博物園區.name: New Pingxi Coal Mine Museum
TW-NWT|新平溪煤礦博物園區.text: A museum built around an old coal mine. Ride the little mine train nicknamed the “one-eyed boy” and relive the mining days.

TW-NWT|淡水漁人碼頭(淡二漁港).name: Tamsui Fisherman's Wharf
TW-NWT|淡水漁人碼頭(淡二漁港).text: A harbor known for its sunsets and Lover's Bridge. Boat rides and boardwalk strolls make it Tamsui's classic date spot.

TW-NWT|新北市立鶯歌陶瓷博物館.name: Yingge Ceramics Museum
TW-NWT|新北市立鶯歌陶瓷博物館.text: Taiwan's first museum devoted to ceramics, telling the story of the pottery town of Yingge. Nearby, you can try your hand at the potter's wheel.

TW-NWT|烏來溫泉.name: Wulai Hot Springs
TW-NWT|烏來溫泉.text: A hot-spring village in a mountain gorge whose name means “hot water” in the Atayal language. Silky waters, a little trolley train and a waterfall, all in one place.

TW-NWT|三峽老街.name: Sanxia Old Street
TW-NWT|三峽老街.text: An old shopping street of red-brick arcades and Baroque-style facades. Famous for its croissants and the carvings of Zushi Temple.

TW-NWT|朱銘美術館.name: Juming Museum
TW-NWT|朱銘美術館.text: An open-air museum that sculptor Ju Ming spent 12 years creating. Huge works from his Taichi series stand among the green hills.

TW-NWT|福隆海水浴場.name: Fulong Beach
TW-NWT|福隆海水浴場.text: A golden beach between a river and the sea, known for its summer sand sculpture festival and the Fulong railway lunch box.

TW-TAO|大溪老街.name: Daxi Old Street
TW-TAO|大溪老街.text: An old street lined with Baroque facades, known for its pressed dried tofu and woodcraft.

TW-TAO|石門水庫.name: Shimen Reservoir
TW-TAO|石門水庫.text: Once the largest reservoir in the Far East. Cycle along the shore or take a boat ride to enjoy the scenery through the seasons.

TW-TAO|拉拉山國家森林遊樂區.name: Lalashan National Forest Recreation Area
TW-TAO|拉拉山國家森林遊樂區.text: A forest of giant trees whose name means “beautiful” in Atayal. Red cypresses as much as a thousand years old rise through the mist.

TW-TAO|慈湖遊客中心.name: Cihu (Two Chiangs Cultural Park)
TW-TAO|慈湖遊客中心.text: A place closely tied to Chiang Kai-shek, known for its park crowded with countless Chiang statues and its changing of the guard.

TW-TAO|角板山行館.name: Jiaobanshan Villa
TW-TAO|角板山行館.text: A former retreat on the Northern Cross-Island Highway, with a wartime tunnel and a plum orchard. In winter it's a favorite spot for plum blossoms.

TW-TAO|小烏來天空步道.name: Xiao Wulai Skywalk
TW-TAO|小烏來天空步道.text: A glass-floored walkway that juts out right above a waterfall. Look down at the gorge and falls beneath your feet for a real thrill.

TW-TAO|桃園忠烈祠暨神社文化園區.name: Taoyuan Shinto Shrine (Martyrs' Shrine)
TW-TAO|桃園忠烈祠暨神社文化園區.text: The most complete Japanese-era Shinto shrine still standing in Taiwan, a serene space built of Taiwanese cypress.

TW-TAO|竹圍漁港.name: Zhuwei Fishing Port
TW-TAO|竹圍漁港.text: A fishing port known for its rainbow arch bridge and fresh seafood market, busy with people who come for seafood rice bowls.

TW-TAO|桃園：大溪老茶廠.name: Daxi Tea Factory
TW-TAO|桃園：大溪老茶廠.text: A tea factory founded in 1926 and since restored. Sip tea in a blue-gray building where old tea-making machines still stand.

TW-TAO|東眼山國家森林遊樂區.name: Dongyanshan National Forest Recreation Area
TW-TAO|東眼山國家森林遊樂區.text: A forest park of cedar woods and old logging relics. Easy trails lead to views over the Taipei Basin.

TW-HSZ|新竹都城隍廟.name: Hsinchu City God Temple
TW-HSZ|新竹都城隍廟.text: A City God temple founded in 1748. The food stalls out front are a mecca for Hsinchu eats like rice noodles and meatball soup.

TW-HSZ|青草湖.name: Qingcao Lake
TW-HSZ|青草湖.text: A quiet lake close to the city, perfect for walking or cycling along the lakeside paths and across the suspension bridge.

TW-HSZ|十八尖山.name: Shibajian Mountain
TW-HSZ|十八尖山.text: A much-loved local hill. Every trailhead gets you to the top in about 20 minutes, which makes it a popular morning walk.

TW-HSZ|南寮運動公園.name: Nanliao Sports Park
TW-HSZ|南寮運動公園.text: A park next to Nanliao Fishing Port and the starting point of a 17 km coastal bike path. A favorite with families.

TW-HSZ|玻璃工藝博物館.name: Hsinchu City Glass Museum
TW-HSZ|玻璃工藝博物館.text: A showcase of glass art in Hsinchu Park, gathering the best of the city's century-old glass industry.

TW-HSZ|新竹市立動物園.name: Hsinchu Zoo
TW-HSZ|新竹市立動物園.text: Taiwan's oldest zoo, reborn after a renovation as a “zoo without cages.” Small, but a gem.

TW-HSZ|迎曦門(東門城).name: Yingxi Gate (East Gate)
TW-HSZ|迎曦門(東門城).text: Built in 1829, it's the only surviving gate of the old Zhuqian city walls. Lit up at night, its plaza becomes a stage for local life.

TW-HSZ|國立新竹生活美學館.name: National Hsinchu Living Arts Center
TW-HSZ|國立新竹生活美學館.text: A restored public hall from a century ago. Exhibitions and cultural events fill its elegant blend of Japanese and Western styles.

TW-HSZ|新竹公園.name: Hsinchu Park
TW-HSZ|新竹公園.text: The city's biggest park. Kids love the huge sandpit and slides, and in spring the cherry trees by the lake burst into bloom.

TW-HSZ|靜心湖.name: Jingxin Lake
TW-HSZ|靜心湖.text: A quiet, peaceful lake inside the Science Park, with Ju Ming's Taichi sculptures standing on its banks.

TW-HSQ|內灣老街.name: Neiwan Old Street
TW-HSQ|內灣老街.text: An old street in the hills at the end of the Neiwan branch line, with Hakka food, a suspension bridge and a retro movie theater.

TW-HSQ|司馬庫斯巨木群步道.name: Smangus Giant Tree Trail
TW-HSQ|司馬庫斯巨木群步道.text: A 5.3 km trail from a remote mountain village known as “God's Tribe” to giant trees as much as a thousand years old.

TW-HSQ|北埔慈天宮.name: Beipu Citian Temple
TW-HSQ|北埔慈天宮.text: The temple at the heart of Beipu Old Street. The lane leading to it is lined with shops selling Hakka lei cha and other Hakka dishes, perfect for snacking as you go.

TW-HSQ|綠世界生態農場.name: Green World Ecological Farm
TW-HSQ|綠世界生態農場.text: A large eco-farm with six themed zones. Walking the alpacas and the bird and butterfly exhibits are big favorites.

TW-HSQ|六福村主題遊樂園.name: Leofoo Village Theme Park
TW-HSQ|六福村主題遊樂園.text: Asia's first theme park to combine a safari with thrill rides. The pools open in summer.

TW-HSQ|尖石鄉原住民文化館.name: Jianshi Indigenous Culture Museum
TW-HSQ|尖石鄉原住民文化館.text: Displays of Atayal homes, hunting gear and clothing. A good starting point for visiting the mountain villages of Jianshi.

TW-HSQ|清泉溫泉.name: Qingquan Hot Spring
TW-HSQ|清泉溫泉.text: A gorge hot spring known since the Japanese era. It's also a historic village where the house in which Zhang Xueliang was held under house arrest still stands.

TW-HSQ|湖口老街.name: Hukou Old Street
TW-HSQ|湖口老街.text: An old street whose red-brick buildings from the 1910s and '20s (the Taisho era) survive almost intact, with beautiful carved shop signs in relief.

TW-HSQ|雪霸休閒農場.name: Shei-Pa Leisure Farm
TW-HSQ|雪霸休閒農場.text: A highland farm at 1,923 m, famous for its sea of clouds, sunrises and early-summer blueberry picking.

TW-HSQ|馬武督探索森林(綠光小學).name: Mawudu Exploring Forest
TW-HSQ|馬武督探索森林(綠光小學).text: A forest theme park dotted with waterfalls and giant trees, also known for the “Green Light School,” a location used in a TV drama.

TW-ILA|太平山國家森林遊樂區.name: Taipingshan National Forest Recreation Area
TW-ILA|太平山國家森林遊樂區.text: A former logging area turned forest kingdom, with the Bong Bong little train, the alpine Cuifeng Lake and hot springs. Its golden autumn beeches are famous, too.

TW-ILA|礁溪蘭花咖啡館.name: Jiaoxi Orchid Café
TW-ILA|礁溪蘭花咖啡館.text: A garden café next to an orchid farm, where you can enjoy coffee surrounded by flowers and greenery.

TW-ILA|冬山河親水公園.name: Dongshan River Water Park
TW-ILA|冬山河親水公園.text: A riverside park whose symbol is a red arch bridge. It's famous as the venue for the summer Yilan International Children's Folklore and Folkgame Festival.

TW-ILA|龜山島.name: Guishan Island (Turtle Island)
TW-ILA|龜山島.text: A turtle-shaped volcanic island in the Pacific. The “Milk Sea,” where the water turns milky white, plus landing tours and whale watching, draw the crowds.

TW-ILA|蘭陽博物館.name: Lanyang Museum
TW-ILA|蘭陽博物館.text: An architectural landmark whose slanted form, modeled on a cuesta, juts out of the water. A great place to learn about Yilan's land and life.

TW-ILA|幾米廣場(丟丟噹森林公園).name: Jimmy Square (Diudiudang Forest)
TW-ILA|幾米廣場(丟丟噹森林公園).text: A plaza that brings to life the world of picture-book artist Jimmy Liao. Its flying-train sculptures are a favorite.

TW-ILA|梅花湖風景區.name: Meihua Lake Scenic Area
TW-ILA|梅花湖風景區.text: A mountain lake shaped like a plum blossom. Cycling the shore and strolling out to the island in the middle are wonderfully peaceful.

TW-ILA|五峰旗風景區.name: Wufengqi Scenic Area
TW-ILA|五峰旗風景區.text: A three-tiered waterfall at the foot of five flag-shaped peaks, the quiet hideaway behind Jiaoxi's hot springs.

TW-ILA|國立傳統藝術中心宜蘭傳藝園區.name: National Center for Traditional Arts (Yilan)
TW-ILA|國立傳統藝術中心宜蘭傳藝園區.text: A theme park where you can try traditional performing arts and crafts. The recreated old street and theater are a delight.

TW-ILA|清水地熱公園.name: Qingshui Geothermal Park
TW-ILA|清水地熱公園.text: A popular park where you can boil eggs and corn in the geothermal water. There's a foot bath, too.

TW-MIA|勝興車站.name: Shengxing Station
TW-MIA|勝興車站.text: A wooden station opened in 1903 at the highest point (402 m) on Taiwan's main north–south railway. The place to start exploring the Old Mountain Line.

TW-MIA|龍騰斷橋、南斷橋.name: Longteng Broken Bridge
TW-MIA|龍騰斷橋、南斷橋.text: A red-brick arch bridge brought down by the great earthquake of 1935. Its surviving pillars, wrapped in greenery, tell its story.

TW-MIA|大湖草莓文化館.name: Dahu Strawberry Culture Museum
TW-MIA|大湖草莓文化館.text: A museum in Dahu, Taiwan's strawberry country. From November to April it's picking season, and the air smells sweet.

TW-MIA|三義木雕博物館.name: Sanyi Wood Sculpture Museum
TW-MIA|三義木雕博物館.text: Taiwan's only public museum devoted to wood carving, surrounded by a town full of carving studios and shops.

TW-MIA|飛牛牧場.name: Flying Cow Ranch
TW-MIA|飛牛牧場.text: A peaceful ranch where cows and sheep graze on rolling hills, with lots for families to try, like milking and feeding the animals.

TW-MIA|南庄老街(桂花巷).name: Nanzhuang Old Street (Osmanthus Lane)
TW-MIA|南庄老街(桂花巷).text: An old lane in a Hakka mountain town, lined with shops selling honey-preserved osmanthus and handmade noodles.

TW-MIA|泰安溫泉區.name: Tai'an Hot Springs
TW-MIA|泰安溫泉區.text: A valley hot spring discovered by the Atayal in 1908. A quiet spa town cradled by mountains.

TW-MIA|明德水庫風景區.name: Mingde Reservoir Scenic Area
TW-MIA|明德水庫風景區.text: A lush reservoir in the hills, where a suspension bridge takes you out to an island in the lake.

TW-MIA|觀霧國家森林遊樂區.name: Guanwu National Forest Recreation Area
TW-MIA|觀霧國家森林遊樂區.text: A misty high-mountain forest, famous for its giant-tree trail and views of the Holy Ridge of the Xueshan Range.

TW-MIA|后厝龍鳳宮.name: Houcuo Longfeng Temple
TW-MIA|后厝龍鳳宮.text: A Mazu temple founded in 1836, known for its giant Mazu statue and intricate carvings.

TW-TXG|高美濕地_高美野生動物保護區.name: Gaomei Wetlands
TW-TXG|高美濕地_高美野生動物保護區.text: A vast wetland famous for its boardwalk with views of wind turbines and the setting sun. One of Taiwan's signature sunset spots.

TW-TXG|谷關遊客中心暨入關博物館.name: Guguan Visitor Center
TW-TXG|谷關遊客中心暨入關博物館.text: The gateway to Guguan, a hot-spring town on the Central Cross-Island Highway. A small museum worth a stop before your soak.

TW-TXG|武陵國家森林遊樂區.name: Wuling National Forest Recreation Area
TW-TXG|武陵國家森林遊樂區.text: A forest at 1,800 m. This mountain resort is famous for spring cherry blossoms, autumn leaves and the Formosan landlocked salmon that lives in its streams.

TW-TXG|大雪山國家森林遊樂區.name: Dasyueshan National Forest Recreation Area
TW-TXG|大雪山國家森林遊樂區.text: Seas of clouds, starry skies and sacred red cypresses. A birdwatching haven where you might spot muntjacs and Mikado pheasants.

TW-TXG|梧棲觀光漁港.name: Wuqi Fishing Harbor
TW-TXG|梧棲觀光漁港.text: Central Taiwan's biggest tourist fish market, where you can pick out fresh-off-the-boat seafood and have it cooked on the spot. Pair it with a visit to Gaomei Wetlands.

TW-TXG|東豐自行車綠廊.name: Dongfeng Bikeway
TW-TXG|東豐自行車綠廊.text: Taiwan's first bike path built on a disused rail line (13.6 km), passing old platforms and a fault park.

TW-TXG|八仙山國家森林遊樂區.name: Basianshan National Forest Recreation Area
TW-TXG|八仙山國家森林遊樂區.text: Once one of Taiwan's three great logging areas. Easy trails follow the traces of the timber era.

TW-TXG|八仙山自然教育中心.name: Basianshan Nature Education Center
TW-TXG|八仙山自然教育中心.text: A center for learning about forest ecology and logging history, with plenty of guided tours and hands-on programs.

TW-TXG|東勢林業文化園區.name: Dongshi Forestry Culture Park
TW-TXG|東勢林業文化園區.text: A park that preserves a large former sawmill. Its huge wooden mill and log pond recall the golden age of forestry.

TW-TXG|萬和宮.name: Wanhe Temple
TW-TXG|萬和宮.text: Founded in 1684, it's Taichung's oldest temple. It honors Mazu and keeps alive the history of the old Litoudian street.

TW-CHA|鹿港老街.name: Lukang Old Street
TW-CHA|鹿港老街.text: One of Taiwan's best-preserved old townscapes, still showing traces of its heyday as a trading port 300 years ago.

TW-CHA|鹿港天后宮.name: Lukang Tianhou Temple
TW-CHA|鹿港天后宮.text: The only temple in Taiwan with a Mazu statue brought from her ancestral temple on Meizhou. Its carved decoration is the finest in Taiwan.

TW-CHA|1895八卦山抗日保台史蹟館.name: Baguashan 1895 Battle Memorial Hall
TW-CHA|1895八卦山抗日保台史蹟館.text: A museum about the 1895 Battle of Baguashan against Japanese forces. It sits in the Great Buddha Scenic Area, with views across Changhua City.

TW-CHA|王功蚵藝文化館.name: Wanggong Oyster Culture Center
TW-CHA|王功蚵藝文化館.text: A cultural center that turns oyster shells into art and tells the story of life in Wanggong, an oyster-farming town.

TW-CHA|田尾公路花園.name: Tianwei Highway Garden
TW-CHA|田尾公路花園.text: Taiwan's biggest flower-growing area. More than 140 nurseries line the roads, and cycling past the flower fields is a joy.

TW-CHA|扇形車庫.name: Changhua Roundhouse
TW-CHA|扇形車庫.text: Taiwan's only surviving fan-shaped engine shed. Watch locomotives turn on the turntable up close. A must for rail fans.

TW-CHA|鹿港龍山寺.name: Lukang Longshan Temple
TW-CHA|鹿港龍山寺.text: A national historic site founded in the late Ming or early Qing. The octagonal caisson ceiling above its stage is hailed as the pinnacle of Taiwanese wooden architecture.

TW-CHA|展壯台大蘭園.name: Taida Orchid Farm
TW-CHA|展壯台大蘭園.text: A large farm growing moth orchids and other varieties. You can tour the farm and buy orchids to take home.

TW-CHA|郁文齋燈藝工作室.name: Yu Wen Zhai Lantern Studio
TW-CHA|郁文齋燈藝工作室.text: A studio that hand-paints traditional lanterns using watercolor and ink-wash techniques, creating a style of lantern light all its own.

TW-CHA|台明將台灣玻璃館.name: Taiwan Glass Gallery
TW-CHA|台明將台灣玻璃館.text: A glass art gallery known for its mirrored “Golden Tunnel” and the glass Mazu temple next door.

TW-NAN|日月潭伊達邵碼頭商圈.name: Ita Thao Pier, Sun Moon Lake
TW-NAN|日月潭伊達邵碼頭商圈.text: A lakeside village of the Thao people on Sun Moon Lake. It's the hub for boat cruises and the ropeway, and the place to try local specialties.

TW-NAN|清境農場.name: Cingjing Farm
TW-NAN|清境農場.text: A highland ranch at 1,748 m. From green hills where sheep graze, gaze out over a sea of clouds. A “paradise above the mist.”

TW-NAN|溪頭自然教育園區.name: Xitou Nature Education Area
TW-NAN|溪頭自然教育園區.text: A haven for forest bathing among tall cedars. University Pond, with its bamboo bridge, is as pretty as a painting.

TW-NAN|九族文化村.name: Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village
TW-NAN|九族文化村.text: A theme park that pairs Indigenous culture with thrill rides. It connects directly to the Sun Moon Lake Ropeway and is a cherry blossom hotspot in spring.

TW-NAN|猴探井天空之橋.name: Houtanjing Sky Bridge
TW-NAN|猴探井天空之橋.text: A suspension bridge that curves across a valley like a smile. Romantic when it lights up at dusk.

TW-NAN|集集攔河堰.name: Jiji Weir
TW-NAN|集集攔河堰.text: Taiwan's largest intake weir, spanning the Zhuoshui River and holding back a broad, sweeping expanse of water.

TW-NAN|南投：臺灣菸酒(股)公司埔里觀光酒廠.name: Puli Brewery
TW-NAN|南投：臺灣菸酒(股)公司埔里觀光酒廠.text: A Shaoxing wine brewery in Puli, a town famous for its water. Tour the wine culture museum and try dishes made with the wine.

TW-NAN|奧萬大國家森林遊樂區.name: Aowanda National Forest Recreation Area
TW-NAN|奧萬大國家森林遊樂區.text: Taiwan's top spot for fall foliage. In late autumn, maples paint the hills red around the suspension bridges that span the gorge.

TW-NAN|鳶峰觀景台(合歡山暗空公園).name: Yuanfeng Viewing Platform (Hehuanshan Dark Sky Park)
TW-NAN|鳶峰觀景台(合歡山暗空公園).text: A dark sky park certified by the International Dark-Sky Association. High in the mountains, far from light pollution, the sky is full of stars.

TW-NAN|奧萬大自然教育中心.name: Aowanda Nature Education Center
TW-NAN|奧萬大自然教育中心.text: A center running nature programs in forests of pine and maple, where you can feel the pulse of the forest with all five senses.

TW-YUN|北港朝天宮.name: Beigang Chaotian Temple
TW-YUN|北港朝天宮.text: Regarded as the head temple of Mazu worship in Taiwan. Its festival in the third lunar month, the Beigang Mazu procession, is a nationally designated important folk custom.

TW-YUN|劍湖山世界主題樂園.name: Janfusun Fancyworld
TW-YUN|劍湖山世界主題樂園.text: The biggest amusement park in central and southern Taiwan, with a giant Ferris wheel, thrill rides and VR attractions.

TW-YUN|古坑情人橋.name: Gukeng Lovers' Bridge
TW-YUN|古坑情人橋.text: A V-shaped suspension bridge in Huashan, Gukeng's coffee country. Only two people can cross at a time, which makes it a thrilling bridge for couples.

TW-YUN|草嶺地質生態國小.name: Caoling Geological Ecology Elementary School
TW-YUN|草嶺地質生態國小.text: A rebuilt school designed to blend into the surrounding geology. The mountain views from its terrace and the stargazing are the big draws.

TW-YUN|西螺大橋.name: Xiluo Bridge
TW-YUN|西螺大橋.text: A red steel bridge that was the longest in the Far East when it was finished in 1952. It stretches about 2 km across the Zhuoshui River.

TW-YUN|雲林布袋戲館.name: Yunlin Glove Puppetry Museum
TW-YUN|雲林布袋戲館.text: A museum in Yunlin, the home of budaixi glove puppetry, showing the art in all its forms, from traditional to contemporary.

TW-YUN|古坑綠色隧道.name: Gukeng Green Tunnel
TW-YUN|古坑綠色隧道.text: A 2 km green tunnel formed by rows of 50-year-old mango trees. People come for the market and picnics in the shade.

TW-YUN|冠弦吉他樂器行.name: Guan Xian Guitar Workshop
TW-YUN|冠弦吉他樂器行.text: One of the few workshops left in Taiwan where guitars are still made by hand, every instrument crafted one at a time.

TW-YUN|虎尾厝沙龍.name: Huwei Salon
TW-YUN|虎尾厝沙龍.text: A book café in a 70-year-old house that mixes Japanese and Western styles. Huwei's cultural salon.

TW-YUN|Gem Shop真金店.name: Gem Shop
TW-YUN|Gem Shop真金店.text: A long-established jeweler turned a former clinic into this lifestyle shop, a small corner of good taste on a Huwei street.

TW-CYI|阿里山林業村暨檜意森活村.name: Alishan Forestry Village & Hinoki Village
TW-CYI|阿里山林業村暨檜意森活村.text: Japanese-style cypress staff housing that was the base of Alishan's logging industry. Twenty-eight buildings have been reborn as a creative village with the feel of Kyoto.

TW-CYI|阿里山林業鐵路.name: Alishan Forest Railway
TW-CYI|阿里山林業鐵路.text: A century-old forest railway climbing from 30 m to 2,216 m above sea level, through forests of three climate zones. One of the world's great mountain lines.

TW-CYI|射日塔.name: Sun Shooting Tower
TW-CYI|射日塔.text: The city's landmark tower in Chiayi Park. The observation deck gives you a 360-degree view over the city.

TW-CYI|蘭潭月影潭心.name: “Moon Shadow” at Lantan Lake
TW-CYI|蘭潭月影潭心.text: A lake said to have been dug by the Dutch 300 years ago. The lakeside art installation “Moon Shadow” is very photogenic.

TW-CYI|嘉義公園.name: Chiayi Park
TW-CYI|嘉義公園.text: A century-old park shaded by ancient trees and dotted with the Sun Shooting Tower, a Confucius temple and a history museum. A favorite place for locals to unwind.

TW-CYI|森林之歌.name: Song of the Forest
TW-CYI|森林之歌.text: A wooden art tower inspired by sacred trees and the forest railway, magical when it's lit up at night.

TW-CYI|KANO園區.name: KANO Park
TW-CYI|KANO園區.text: A memorial park for the Chiayi Agriculture and Forestry School baseball team made famous by the film KANO, celebrating this baseball town's pride.

TW-CYI|檜意森活村.name: Hinoki Village
TW-CYI|檜意森活村.text: Cypress-built Japanese houses in front of Beimen Station. Browsing the shops and trying on a kimono are popular.

TW-CYI|中正公園.name: Zhongzheng Park (Chiayi)
TW-CYI|中正公園.text: A downtown plaza on the site of the old public hall, and a green stage for events and outdoor shows.

TW-CYI|嘉義文化創意產業園區.name: Chiayi Cultural and Creative Industries Park
TW-CYI|嘉義文化創意產業園區.text: A creative park in what was Taiwan's oldest sorghum liquor factory. The old factory buildings recall the city's days as a liquor capital.

TW-CYQ|阿里山國家森林遊樂區.name: Alishan National Forest Recreation Area
TW-CYQ|阿里山國家森林遊樂區.text: Taiwan's most famous mountain resort, home to the “five wonders”: the forest railway, sacred trees, the sea of clouds, sunrise and sunset glow.

TW-CYQ|奮起湖(南側)杉林棧道.name: Fenqihu Cedar Boardwalk
TW-CYQ|奮起湖(南側)杉林棧道.text: A boardwalk through the cedar groves of Fenqihu, the village famous for its railway lunch boxes. A lovely walk through the misty forest.

TW-CYQ|太平雲梯.name: Taiping Suspension Bridge
TW-CYQ|太平雲梯.text: At about 1,000 m, it's Taiwan's highest suspension bridge, 281 m long. It feels like walking above the clouds.

TW-CYQ|高跟鞋教堂.name: High-Heel Wedding Church
TW-CYQ|高跟鞋教堂.text: A giant high-heeled shoe made of 320 panes of glass, recognized by Guinness as one of the world's largest glass structures.

TW-CYQ|東石漁人碼頭.name: Dongshi Fisherman's Wharf
TW-CYQ|東石漁人碼頭.text: A harbor park lined with colorful huts and a man-made beach. Don't leave without trying the local oyster dishes.

TW-CYQ|鰲鼓濕地森林園區.name: Aogu Wetland Forest Park
TW-CYQ|鰲鼓濕地森林園區.text: Reclaimed land that has become a paradise for migratory birds. In winter, countless birds gather here, black-faced spoonbills among them.

TW-CYQ|達娜伊谷自然生態公園.name: Tanayiku Natural Ecological Park
TW-CYQ|達娜伊谷自然生態公園.text: In the Tsou language, “the valley where you forget your sorrows.” Fish swarm in a stream the community has fought to protect.

TW-CYQ|觸口自然教育中心.name: Chukou Nature Education Center
TW-CYQ|觸口自然教育中心.text: An ecology center on the road up to Alishan, where the old trees of its “Tree Bank” greet you.

TW-CYQ|阿里山生態教育館.name: Alishan Ecology Education Center
TW-CYQ|阿里山生態教育館.text: An ecology museum in a converted old work station, with a forestry history exhibit. Learn about Alishan's nature and history.

TW-CYQ|大林慢城發展協會.name: Dalin Slow City
TW-CYQ|大林慢城發展協會.text: A town certified by Cittaslow International. Old movie theaters and open countryside make it perfect for an unhurried trip.

TW-TNN|赤崁樓.name: Chihkan Tower
TW-TNN|赤崁樓.text: Fort Provintia, built by the Dutch in 1652. The historic site that best captures the old capital of Tainan.

TW-TNN|安平古堡.name: Anping Old Fort
TW-TNN|安平古堡.text: The site of Fort Zeelandia, built in 1624. Known as the place Koxinga drove out the Dutch, it's where Taiwan's story begins.

TW-TNN|億載金城 (二鯤鯓砲台).name: Eternal Golden Castle
TW-TNN|億載金城 (二鯤鯓砲台).text: A Western-style fort completed in 1876. Its moat-ringed red-brick gateway is impressive.

TW-TNN|奇美博物館.name: Chimei Museum
TW-TNN|奇美博物館.text: A private museum that looks like a European palace, with vast collections of Western paintings, musical instruments, and arms and armor.

TW-TNN|四草綠色隧道.name: Sicao Green Tunnel
TW-TNN|四草綠色隧道.text: Mangroves arch over the waterway in “Taiwan's mini Amazon.” Gliding through on a raft over mirror-still water is magical.

TW-TNN|神農街.name: Shennong Street
TW-TNN|神農街.text: A lane that still evokes the Qing-era port town. At night, when the lanterns glow, hop between bars set in old houses.

TW-TNN|孔廟文化園區「臺南孔子廟」.name: Tainan Confucius Temple
TW-TNN|孔廟文化園區「臺南孔子廟」.text: Founded in 1665, it was Taiwan's first Confucius temple. A plaque proclaims it the “First Academy of Taiwan,” and red walls enclose a serene space.

TW-TNN|井仔腳瓦盤鹽田.name: Jingzaijiao Tile-paved Salt Fields
TW-TNN|井仔腳瓦盤鹽田.text: The oldest surviving tile-paved salt fields, famous for sunsets reflected in their mosaic of salt pans.

TW-TNN|關子嶺風景區(泥漿溫泉).name: Guanziling Hot Springs
TW-TNN|關子嶺風景區(泥漿溫泉).text: Taiwan's only mud hot spring. Known for its silky dark water and the “Water and Fire Cave,” where flames burn above flowing water.

TW-TNN|安平樹屋.name: Anping Tree House
TW-TNN|安平樹屋.text: An abandoned warehouse swallowed by banyan trees. With roots covering the walls, it feels like a castle in the sky.

TW-KHH|旗津天后宮.name: Cijin Tianhou Temple
TW-KHH|旗津天后宮.text: Founded in 1673, one of Taiwan's earliest Mazu temples, and the spiritual heart of Cijin Island, which you reach by ferry.

TW-KHH|佛光山.name: Fo Guang Shan
TW-KHH|佛光山.text: A holy site of Taiwanese Buddhism founded by Master Hsing Yun. The huge Buddha Museum and giant Buddha are on an awe-inspiring scale.

TW-KHH|西子灣蔣介石行館.name: Former Chiang Kai-shek Residence, Sizihwan
TW-KHH|西子灣蔣介石行館.text: A 1935 building blending Japanese and Western styles, set amid the greenery of National Sun Yat-sen University.

TW-KHH|愛河.name: Love River
TW-KHH|愛河.text: A romantic river flowing through downtown Kaohsiung. Night cruises and riverside cafés are classics.

TW-KHH|田寮月世界.name: Tianliao Moon World
TW-KHH|田寮月世界.text: Badlands eroded into a lunar landscape. Lit up at night, it's otherworldly.

TW-KHH|壽山國家自然公園.name: Shoushan National Nature Park
TW-KHH|壽山國家自然公園.text: A green mountain looking down on the city and harbor. Monkeys roam its forests on old coral reef, and it's ideal for hiking.

TW-KHH|打狗英國領事館文化園區.name: British Consulate at Takao
TW-KHH|打狗英國領事館文化園區.text: A red-brick consulate on a hill, built in 1879. Afternoon tea with a view of the harbor and the Sizihwan sunset is a favorite.

TW-KHH|凝聚的綠寶石-R4高雄國際機場站.name: “Green Gem” at Kaohsiung International Airport Station
TW-KHH|凝聚的綠寶石-R4高雄國際機場站.text: One of the world's largest glass artworks decorates this metro airport station, glowing green like a jewel.

TW-KHH|曾文忠美術館.name: Tseng Wen-chung Art Museum
TW-KHH|曾文忠美術館.text: A museum of works by Tseng Wen-chung, a painter from the Hakka town of Meinong, celebrating the beauty of his home region.

TW-KHH|永安老街.name: Yong'an Old Street, Meinong
TW-KHH|永安老街.text: A 200-year-old street in the Hakka town of Meinong. Traditional houses, oil-paper umbrellas and the aroma of Hakka noodles.

TW-PIF|墾丁國家森林遊樂區.name: Kenting National Forest Recreation Area
TW-PIF|墾丁國家森林遊樂區.text: A subtropical forest on uplifted coral reef. Explore limestone caves and take in the ocean from the lookout tower.

TW-PIF|東港魚市場.name: Donggang Fish Market
TW-PIF|東港魚市場.text: A harbor market famous for its Pacific bluefin tuna catch. Lively auctions and fresh sashimi are the draws.

TW-PIF|霧臺遊憩區.name: Wutai (Rukai village)
TW-PIF|霧臺遊憩區.text: A mountaintop Rukai village wrapped in mist and cloud. Slate houses and the hundred-pacer snake motif speak of its pride.

TW-PIF|雙流國家森林遊樂區.name: Shuangliu National Forest Recreation Area
TW-PIF|雙流國家森林遊樂區.text: A streamside trail leads to what's called “Taiwan's second most beautiful waterfall.” Breathe in the cool, fresh air of the banyan forest.

TW-PIF|屏東縣民公園.name: Pingtung County Park
TW-PIF|屏東縣民公園.text: A park reborn from an old sugar factory, where rust-colored ruins and illuminated waterfronts create a kind of industrial beauty.

TW-PIF|屏東縣立圖書館總館.name: Pingtung County Library
TW-PIF|屏東縣立圖書館總館.text: Dubbed “Taiwan's most beautiful library,” it stands in a forest, so you can read surrounded by greenery through the glass.

TW-PIF|屏東美術館.name: Pingtung Art Museum
TW-PIF|屏東美術館.text: An art museum in a converted early postwar government building, a space that holds the town's memories.

TW-PIF|屏東書院.name: Pingtung Confucian Academy (Confucius Temple)
TW-PIF|屏東書院.text: An academy and Confucius temple founded in 1814. Its lecture hall and shrine survive, the birthplace of learning in Pingtung.

TW-PIF|邱姓河南堂忠實第.name: Qiu Family Henan Hall
TW-PIF|邱姓河南堂忠實第.text: A century-old courtyard house that tells the history of the Hakka Liudui settlements.

TW-PIF|屏東藝術館.name: Pingtung Art Center
TW-PIF|屏東藝術館.text: Long the county's cultural center, it's a home for music and the performing arts.

TW-HUA|太魯閣牌樓.name: Taroko Gate
TW-HUA|太魯閣牌樓.text: The palace-style archway at the entrance to the Central Cross-Island Highway. Note: parts of the gorge itself remain closed because of earthquake damage.

TW-HUA|七星潭海岸風景特定區.name: Qixingtan Beach
TW-HUA|七星潭海岸風景特定區.text: A crescent-shaped pebble beach. Blue sea, glossy black stones and the mountains behind make this Hualien's most beautiful stretch of coast.

TW-HUA|清水斷崖.name: Qingshui Cliffs
TW-HUA|清水斷崖.text: Marble cliffs plunging straight into the Pacific along the Suhua Highway. One of the Eight Views of Taiwan.

TW-HUA|鯉魚潭環潭自行車道.name: Liyu Lake Bike Path
TW-HUA|鯉魚潭環潭自行車道.text: A bike route all the way around the lake in dappled shade, also known for firefly watching at night.

TW-HUA|瑞穗牧場.name: Ruisui Ranch
TW-HUA|瑞穗牧場.text: A ranch where you can feed dairy cows and ostriches. Desserts made with fresh milk are the specialty.

TW-HUA|六十石山金針花海.name: Liushidan Mountain Daylily Fields
TW-HUA|六十石山金針花海.text: In August and September the whole mountain turns orange with daylilies, a summer tradition in the East Rift Valley.

TW-HUA|林田山林業文化園區.name: Lintianshan Forestry Culture Park
TW-HUA|林田山林業文化園區.text: A logging base once known as “Morisaka.” Its Japanese-style dorms and forest railway survive intact.

TW-HUA|石梯坪遊憩區.name: Shitiping
TW-HUA|石梯坪遊憩區.text: A sea-carved terrace of strange rocks. Potholes and tide pools make it fun to look for sea life.

TW-HUA|遠雄海洋公園.name: Farglory Ocean Park
TW-HUA|遠雄海洋公園.text: A marine theme park between the mountains and the sea. Dolphin shows and the gondola are favorites.

TW-HUA|雲山水植物農場.name: Yunshanshui
TW-HUA|雲山水植物農場.text: Its “Dream Lake” mirrors rows of palms and the silhouettes of mountains. One of Hualien's top photo spots.

TW-TTT|三仙台風景區.name: Sanxiantai
TW-TTT|三仙台風景區.text: An eight-arch footbridge snakes like a dragon out to the island. A symbol of the east coast and a famous sunrise spot.

TW-TTT|伯朗大道.name: Mr. Brown Avenue
TW-TTT|伯朗大道.text: A road with no power poles running through golden rice fields, home to the “Takeshi Kaneshiro tree” made famous by a TV commercial.

TW-TTT|鹿野高台.name: Luye Highland
TW-TTT|鹿野高台.text: A plateau looking over the rift valley. In July and August it hosts Taiwan's biggest hot-air balloon festival.

TW-TTT|知本國家森林遊樂區.name: Zhiben National Forest Recreation Area
TW-TTT|知本國家森林遊樂區.text: A subtropical forest next to Zhiben Hot Springs, with century-old banyans and soothing forest trails.

TW-TTT|白色恐怖綠島紀念園區.name: Green Island White Terror Memorial Park
TW-TTT|白色恐怖綠島紀念園區.text: A former prison camp for political prisoners from the martial-law era. Set against a beautiful sea, it preserves an important chapter in Taiwan's human rights history.

TW-TTT|蘭嶼氣象站.name: Lanyu Weather Station
TW-TTT|蘭嶼氣象站.text: A white weather station built during the Japanese era. Bullet holes in its walls tell its history, and it looks out over the whole island.

TW-TTT|加路蘭遊憩區.name: Jialulan Recreation Area
TW-TTT|加路蘭遊憩區.text: Its name means “place to wash your hair” in the Amis language. Driftwood art dots a seaside meadow, a lovely spot for watching the moon.

TW-TTT|富岡地質公園 (小野柳).name: Xiaoyeliu (Fugang Geopark)
TW-TTT|富岡地質公園 (小野柳).text: A coastal geopark nicknamed “Little Yehliu” for rock formations like those at Yehliu.

TW-TTT|臺東森林公園.name: Taitung Forest Park
TW-TTT|臺東森林公園.text: A 280-hectare green space right next to the city. Cycling around the mirror-like Pipa Lake is the thing to do.

TW-TTT|知本自然教育中心.name: Zhiben Nature Education Center
TW-TTT|知本自然教育中心.text: A center for learning about tropical monsoon forest ecology, with hot-spring steam drifting nearby.

TW-PEN|雙心石滬.name: Twin Hearts Stone Weir
TW-PEN|雙心石滬.text: A heart-shaped fish trap of stacked basalt, born of generations of know-how. Penghu's most romantic sight.

TW-PEN|澎湖跨海大橋.name: Penghu Great Bridge
TW-PEN|澎湖跨海大橋.text: A 2.5 km bridge over a fast-flowing strait, linking Baisha and Xiyu islands. A symbol of Penghu.

TW-PEN|吉貝嶼.name: Jibei Island
TW-PEN|吉貝嶼.text: The largest island in Penghu's northern waters. A golden sandbar reaches into the sea, and it buzzes as a water sports paradise.

TW-PEN|二崁傳統聚落保存區.name: Erkan Historic Village
TW-PEN|二崁傳統聚落保存區.text: Taiwan's first protected traditional village. Old houses serve as small museums, and the scent of almond tea drifts through the lanes.

TW-PEN|山水沙灘.name: Shanshui Beach
TW-PEN|山水沙灘.text: A 200 m beach of green vines, golden sand and blue sea, popular for surfing too.

TW-PEN|風櫃洞.name: Fenggui Cave
TW-PEN|風櫃洞.text: Waves crash into a basalt sea cave with a thundering roar. “Listening to the waves at Fenggui” is one of Penghu's famous sights.

TW-PEN|大菓葉柱狀玄武岩.name: Daguoye Columnar Basalt
TW-PEN|大菓葉柱狀玄武岩.text: A wall of columnar basalt uncovered by chance during construction work. Reflected in the pools after rain, it's stunning.

TW-PEN|澎湖輪碼頭.name: Penghu Ferry Terminal
TW-PEN|澎湖輪碼頭.text: The gateway for ferries between Taiwan's main island and Penghu. If you're coming by sea, your trip starts here.

TW-PEN|澎湖生活博物館.name: Penghu Living Museum
TW-PEN|澎湖生活博物館.text: A museum that recreates Penghu's daily life and maritime culture through dioramas and film.

TW-PEN|目斗嶼.name: Mudou Islet
TW-PEN|目斗嶼.text: A black-and-white striped lighthouse on a tiny island, guiding ships past the reefs for more than a century since the Qing era.

TW-KIN|莒光樓.name: Juguang Tower
TW-KIN|莒光樓.text: Kinmen's landmark tower, built in traditional gate-tower style. From the top you can see across Jincheng and out to sea.

TW-KIN|翟山坑道.name: Zhaishan Tunnel
TW-KIN|翟山坑道.text: An underground waterway cut through granite to hide boats during wartime, also famous as the venue for a tunnel music festival.

TW-KIN|水頭57地號洋樓(僑鄉文化展示館).name: Shuitou Overseas Chinese Culture Exhibition Hall
TW-KIN|水頭57地號洋樓(僑鄉文化展示館).text: A Western-style house next to Deyue Tower, telling the stories of Kinmen people who emigrated to Southeast Asia.

TW-KIN|山后民俗文化村.name: Shanhou Folk Culture Village
TW-KIN|山后民俗文化村.text: Eighteen southern Fujian-style houses in neat rows. Kinmen's most complete traditional village.

TW-KIN|獅山砲陣地.name: Shishan Howitzer Base
TW-KIN|獅山砲陣地.text: A howitzer position inside a tunnel, where a dramatic gun-drill demonstration brings wartime memories back to life.

TW-KIN|慈湖.name: Cihu Lake (Kinmen)
TW-KIN|慈湖.text: A lake created by a military embankment, now a haven for wild birds and famous for its sunsets.

TW-KIN|建功嶼.name: Jiangong Islet
TW-KIN|建功嶼.text: A tiny island you walk to along a stone path that appears only at low tide. Sunsets and sculptures of oyster farmers make a perfect picture.

TW-KIN|陳景蘭洋樓.name: Chen Jing-lan Western-style Mansion
TW-KIN|陳景蘭洋樓.text: Built in 1921, Kinmen's largest Western-style mansion, with white arched verandas overlooking Liaoluo Bay.

TW-KIN|清金門鎮總兵署.name: Qing Dynasty Kinmen Garrison Headquarters
TW-KIN|清金門鎮總兵署.text: An almost fully intact Qing-era military headquarters. You can visit this historic building in the evening, too.

TW-KIN|得月樓.name: Deyue Tower
TW-KIN|得月樓.text: A gun tower built in 1931 to guard against bandits. The tallest building in Shuitou Village, it has watched over the island ever since.

TW-LIE|芹壁社區發展協會.name: Qinbi Village
TW-LIE|芹壁社區發展協會.text: Matsu's finest village, with granite stone houses facing the sea. People call it “the Mediterranean of Matsu.”

TW-LIE|南竿北海坑道.name: Beihai Tunnel (Nangan)
TW-LIE|南竿北海坑道.text: An underground military harbor dug through granite. Explore it by rowboat, and on summer nights watch the blue tears glow.

TW-LIE|東引中路客廳.name: Dongyin Zhonglu Parlor
TW-LIE|東引中路客廳.text: The old town of Dongyin, the northernmost island Taiwan governs, telling the story of island life shaped by fishing and the military.

TW-LIE|大漢據點.name: Dahan Stronghold
TW-LIE|大漢據點.text: A coastal defense post carved out of bedrock, with its gun slits and command post left just as they were.

TW-LIE|馬祖境天后宮.name: Matsu Tianhou Temple
TW-LIE|馬祖境天后宮.text: Said to be where Mazu rests, this temple gave the islands their name and is the center of local faith.

TW-LIE|藍眼淚生態館.name: Blue Tears Ecology Museum
TW-LIE|藍眼淚生態館.text: A museum where you can see the blue tears, the glowing night sea, any time of year, and learn how the glow works.

TW-LIE|壁山.name: Bishan
TW-LIE|壁山.text: The highest peak in the Matsu Islands (298 m), with a lookout over Beigan's islands and Qinbi Village.

TW-LIE|津沙聚落.name: Jinsha Village
TW-LIE|津沙聚落.text: A stone-house village nestled by a golden beach. Island life carries on in its lanes, scented with aged rice wine.

TW-LIE|東犬燈塔(東莒島燈塔).name: Dongju Island Lighthouse
TW-LIE|東犬燈塔(東莒島燈塔).text: A white lighthouse built in the Qing era, a heritage site still shining over the sea from its clifftop.

TW-LIE|坤坵沙灘.name: Kunqiu Beach
TW-LIE|坤坵沙灘.text: A beach facing Snake Island. In spring and summer, rare “cross waves” appear, meeting in a grid-like pattern.

food.TW-LIE-2: Misua in aged rice wine (laojiu mianxian)

TW-KEE|周家蔥油餅.text: A pancake shop that opens at 4:30 a.m. and has been going for about 50 years. The scallion dough is griddled, then crisped once more over the flame, so the outside shatters. Have it with a cold soy milk.

TW-KEE|長腳麵食.dish: Noodles with pork knuckle, and old-style dry noodles tossed in lard and fried shallots
TW-KEE|長腳麵食.text: A noodle shop run by three generations for more than 60 years. Flat noodles tossed with lard and fried shallots are an old Keelung taste. The pork knuckle can sell out early, so come in the morning.

TW-KEE|連珍糕餅店.text: A century-old pastry shop near Keelung Station, where locals are said to buy their temple offerings. The taro balls, made with taro from Dajia, come four to a box and are a popular gift.

TW-TPE|賣麵炎仔.dish: Light-broth noodles or rice noodles (qie zai mian), and fried pork (hong shao rou)
TW-TPE|賣麵炎仔.text: A noodle shop tucked into a Dadaocheng alley, run by three generations for over 80 years. It opens at 7 a.m. There's no menu: the owner sizes up your group and puts together a spread of side dishes. The fried pork isn't served until 10 a.m.

TW-TPE|一甲子餐飲.dish: Braised pork belly on rice (kong rou fan) and pork belly buns (gua bao)
TW-TPE|一甲子餐飲.text: A shop right next to Wanhua's Zushi Temple, going for about 60 years. You'll be torn between having the melt-soft pork belly on rice or tucked into a steamed bun. There's also wan gui (savory rice pudding), a recipe the owner learned in Madou, Tainan.

TW-TPE|雙連圓仔湯.dish: Sweet soup with tiny rice balls (yuan zai tang) and fried mochi (shao muaji)
TW-TPE|雙連圓仔湯.text: A dessert shop run by three generations since 1951. Tiny rice balls made only from glutinous rice come in a sweet red bean or peanut soup. The other star is mochi fried in hot oil and rolled in peanut and sesame powder.

TW-TPE|蘇來傳.dish: Ba-wan with pork filling (rou yuan) and steamed taro cake (yu gui)
TW-TPE|蘇來傳.text: A shop in an alley near Lungshan Temple, run by three generations. It moved here from Sanshui Street, into the owner's family home. Order one ba-wan and one taro cake and you'll still get change from NT$100. Add garlic and chili sauce to taste.

TW-NWT|油庫口蚵仔麵線.dish: Oyster and pork intestine vermicelli in a thick, silky broth (o-a mi sua)
TW-NWT|油庫口蚵仔麵線.text: A Banqiao vermicelli shop open since 1986. The oysters and intestines are prepped fresh each day, and the owner makes the fried shallots by hand. Pair it with a grilled sausage from the stall next door: locals call the combo the “full set.”

TW-NWT|今大魯肉飯.dish: Rice with braised diced fatty pork (lu rou fan)
TW-NWT|今大魯肉飯.text: The first name that comes up when people in Sanchong talk about braised pork rice. Diced pork fat is simmered until glossy and tender, then spooned over rice. It opens at 6:30 a.m., so it works for breakfast too.

TW-NWT|永和佳香豆漿.dish: Pepper scallion flatbread (hu jiao cong bing) and soy milk
TW-NWT|永和佳香豆漿.text: A breakfast-only soy milk shop near Minzhi Market. The owner makes everything by hand: the soy milk, the flatbreads, the egg-pancake wrappers, even the xiaolongbao. The pepper scallion flatbread is the star, and there's no fixed time for when it comes out of the oven.

TW-TAO|阿美米干.dish: Yunnan rice noodles (mi gan) in pork-bone broth
TW-TAO|阿美米干.text: Going for more than 40 years near Zhongzhen Market, in a neighborhood where many families have Yunnan roots. The house special, the “A-Mei” bowl, tops flat rice noodles with pork, liver and egg, plus pickled greens and scallions. Opens at 8 a.m.

TW-TAO|鴨肉榮.dish: Boiled duck platter and salted duck (xian shui ya)
TW-TAO|鴨肉榮.text: A duck shop open since 1970, diagonally across from Jingfu Temple, which locals call the “Big Temple.” It's open 24 hours. Dip the duck leg in the house chili sauce and have it with a gingery duck-giblet soup.

TW-TAO|賴媽媽豆花.dish: Douhua (silken tofu pudding) topped with chewy Q-yuan balls
TW-TAO|賴媽媽豆花.text: A douhua shop going for over 50 years that Daxi locals have loved since childhood. It started inside a gymnasium and now has a branch on the old street too. Choose your syrup: sugar, ginger or soy milk.

TW-HSZ|廟口鴨香飯.dish: Smoked duck rice (ya xiang fan), drizzled with duck fat and sauce
TW-HSZ|廟口鴨香飯.text: The duck rice that Hsinchu people have eaten since they were kids, near the City God Temple. Smoked duck goes perfectly with duck fat and the house sauce. Some people add a runny fried egg and mix it all in.

TW-HSZ|東門米粉攤.dish: Thick rice noodle soup with seafood and taro (hai xian yu tou mi fen tang)
TW-HSZ|東門米粉攤.text: A small stall inside East Gate Market. Thick rice noodles in chicken broth come with fried sea bass, fish balls, shrimp and taro. Seats are few, so expect to wait.

TW-HSZ|鷹王肉圓.dish: Ba-wan with red-yeast pork, fried in lard (hong zao rou yuan)
TW-HSZ|鷹王肉圓.text: A ba-wan shop near the air force base, open since 1962. Frying in lard is the house rule, and each one gets a generous pour of sauce and grated garlic. It's not in a busy area, yet there's a line on weekends.

TW-HSQ|ㄤ咕麵.dish: Flat oil noodles tossed in fried-shallot sauce
TW-HSQ|ㄤ咕麵.text: Started as a tiny stall in 1955 and now run by the third generation on Guanxi's old street. Springy flat oil noodles are tossed with chives, bean sprouts and fried-shallot sauce. There are Hakka side dishes too.

TW-HSQ|鄒記菜包.dish: Hakka steamed rice dumplings (cai bao), some with mugwort skins
TW-HSQ|鄒記菜包.text: A cai bao shop carrying on a grandmother's recipe from her stall in front of Beipu's Citian Temple. The skin blends glutinous and regular rice the old way, so it's soft without sticking to your teeth. Mugwort skins are available too.

TW-HSQ|一哥炊粉.dish: Thin steamed rice noodles (chui fen), stir-fried or in soup
TW-HSQ|一哥炊粉.text: A Hakka breakfast spot in Qionglin, going for over 40 years. The thin rice noodles are steamed from indica rice alone, so they taste clearly of rice. Have them stir-fried or in soup, or half and half with flat ban tiao noodles.

TW-ILA|阿娘給的蒜味肉羹.dish: Thick, garlicky soup with pork balls (rou geng)
TW-ILA|阿娘給的蒜味肉羹.text: Founded in 1966. A son now carries on the recipe his mother served for nearly half a century beside a gate in the old town. Both raw and fried garlic perfume this thick soup, and you can add noodles or rice noodles.

TW-ILA|張秀雄米苔目.dish: Thick rice noodles (mi tai mu) in pork-bone broth, a breakfast classic
TW-ILA|張秀雄米苔目.text: A Luodong breakfast shop that opens at 5 a.m. The rice noodles are simple, topped only with fried shallots and celery, and you can get refills of the pork-bone broth. Lots of people add a small plate of pork intestine.

TW-ILA|羅東紅豆湯圓.dish: Red bean soup with rice balls (hong dou tang yuan)
TW-ILA|羅東紅豆湯圓.text: A dessert shop just outside Luodong Night Market, going for over half a century. There are only three things on the menu: red bean soup, rice ball soup, and the two combined. In summer, lots of people order it over ice.

TW-MIA|賴新魁麵館.dish: Hakka flat rice noodles (ban tiao) topped with wontons
TW-MIA|賴新魁麵館.text: A Hakka noodle shop founded in 1945. The signature bowl tops flat rice noodles with wontons, and the aroma of fried red shallots goes beautifully with the clear pork-bone broth.

TW-MIA|江技舊記.dish: Black-pork wonton soup and crystal dumplings
TW-MIA|江技舊記.text: Started in 1949 as a wonton stall in front of a temple and now run by the third generation. The stars are wonton soup scented with black-pork fat and half-moon crystal dumplings.

TW-MIA|金光肉圓.dish: Ba-wan with pork and bamboo shoots in a chewy skin
TW-MIA|金光肉圓.text: A Yuanli shop run by three generations for about 50 years. A chewy skin wraps pork leg and bamboo shoots, then gets a rice-based sauce and a topping of garlic leaves instead of cilantro. That's how they do it here.

TW-TXG|台中肉員.dish: Ba-wan with a thin, oil-dipped skin
TW-TXG|台中肉員.text: Founded in 1933. The menu is just ba-wan, fish ball soup and glass noodle soup. Dipped in oil, the skin is thin and tender. It's listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand.

TW-TXG|阿坤麵.dish: Dry noodles with minced pork and bean sprouts
TW-TXG|阿坤麵.text: Near Second Market for over 50 years. There's just one main dish: yellow noodles with minced pork and bean sprouts, topped with Taichung's own Dongquan chili sauce. Open from morning until lunch, and listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand.

TW-TXG|王塔米糕.dish: Tube-steamed sticky rice with dried oysters (tong zai mi gao)
TW-TXG|王塔米糕.text: The shop that started Qingshui's sticky rice tradition. It's the only place in Qingshui that adds dried oysters to the pork belly. Its other signature is a pork soup with noodles in a clear, unthickened pork-bone broth.

TW-TXG|阿斗伯冷凍芋.text: A street stall going since the 1960s, now run by the third generation. You get three big chunks of taro soaked in old-fashioned syrup. From afternoon until late at night, the line of locals never stops.

TW-CHA|貓鼠麵.dish: Clear-broth noodles topped with chicken rolls and meatballs (san bao mian)
TW-CHA|貓鼠麵.text: Founded in 1921. The name is Taiwanese for “mouse,” the original owner's nickname. Noodles in clear broth come with chicken rolls, shiitake balls and swallow-skin dumplings. After a break, it reopened in August 2025.

TW-CHA|阿泉爌肉飯.dish: Braised pork leg on rice (kong rou fan)
TW-CHA|阿泉爌肉飯.text: A Changhua breakfast spot going for more than 80 years. Skin-on pork leg is braised and laid over rice in one big slab. It opens at 7 a.m. and often sells out before noon, so get there before 9.

TW-CHA|北斗肉圓生.text: A Beidou ba-wan institution run by five generations since 1898. The skin, made from ground rice and sweet potato starch, wraps a filling with bamboo shoots. Look for the red stall out front. The sticky rice is popular too.

TW-NAN|阿章意麵.dish: Nantou yi mian noodles tossed with minced pork
TW-NAN|阿章意麵.text: A shop in a Nantou City market, going for about 50 years. Local yi mian noodles, made without a drop of water, are tossed with lean, salty minced pork. Many regulars have been coming since they were kids.

TW-NAN|李仔哥爌肉飯.dish: Braised pork belly on rice (kong rou fan)
TW-NAN|李仔哥爌肉飯.text: A Puli institution said to date back to 1979. It opens at 6 a.m., so locals come for breakfast. The signature is rice topped with braised pork belly in layers of fat and lean, and the pork chop rice sells out early.

TW-NAN|榕樹下扣仔嗲.text: Under a huge banyan tree for over 60 years. There's no sign: the tree is your landmark. The classic order here is oyster fritters with fried meat, sticky-rice sausage and pork blood soup.

TW-NAN|百年廟口肉圓.dish: Ba-wan with Zhushan winter bamboo shoots
TW-NAN|百年廟口肉圓.text: A long-running shop that started as a stall across from Lianxing Temple, Zhushan's Mazu temple. The skin is made from Zhushan's red sweet potato starch and wraps pork and local winter bamboo shoots before being fried in low-temperature oil. Closed Thursdays and Sundays.

TW-YUN|老受鴨肉飯.dish: Shredded duck on rice (ya rou fan)
TW-YUN|老受鴨肉飯.text: Opened in 1960 and now run by the second generation. Meat from ducks raised for more than 100 days is shredded over rice and finished with a special sauce. People who've moved away from Beigang stop in every time they come home.

TW-YUN|三角大水餃.dish: Big triangular dumplings in sweet potato starch skins
TW-YUN|三角大水餃.text: A shop behind Xiluo's East Market that always has a line. Pork and bamboo shoots are wrapped in triangles of sweet potato starch dough and steamed. Have them dry with the homemade sweet-and-spicy sauce, or in pork-bone broth with Xiluo soy sauce.

TW-YUN|長興圓仔冰.dish: Shaved ice with rice balls (yuan zai bing) and hot mochi
TW-YUN|長興圓仔冰.text: A dessert shop near Douliu's East Market, run by the same family for generations. In summer it serves shaved ice with rice balls; in winter, warm rice ball soup. The mochi and rice balls are made fresh daily, and the peanut and sesame mochi is popular too.

TW-CYI|王家祖傳本產牛雜湯.text: A beef offal soup stall inside East Market, run by four generations. From 6 a.m., people come for breakfast: a light, sweet soup with heart and tripe. It closes soon after midday.

TW-CYI|阿溪雞肉飯.text: A breakfast-only shop going since 1973. Instead of shredded meat, it uses diced chicken, eaten with chicken fat and fried shallots. Regulars order the off-menu sliced chicken rice and a soft-boiled duck egg.

TW-CYI|阿娥豆漿豆花.text: A douhua shop beside Wenhua Road Night Market, going for more than 60 years. Pouring on soy milk instead of syrup is how Chiayi does it. It's topped with peanuts cooked in-house, and some people add a fried dough stick on the side.

TW-CYQ|新港鴨肉羹.text: Since 1966 near Fengtian Temple, with just one thing on the menu: thick duck soup. The duck and bamboo shoots are stir-fried over high heat before simmering, which gives it a toasty aroma. No rice or noodles come with it.

TW-CYQ|麻糬棟.dish: Mochi filled with savory mung bean paste
TW-CYQ|麻糬棟.text: A mochi shop in Puzi First Market since 1936. It's made from whole rice, not flour, and filled with a lightly salty mung bean paste mixed with sugar and peanuts. Choose a white or purple-rice skin.

TW-CYQ|虎兒油飯.dish: Sticky rice steamed in bamboo baskets (you fan)
TW-CYQ|虎兒油飯.text: A Puzi sticky rice shop that opens in the late afternoon. The classic order is sticky rice steamed in bamboo baskets with a thick pork soup. Going for more than 60 years, it's a taste of home for Puzi locals.

TW-TNN|福泰飯桌第三代.dish: Minced pork rice with the day's side dishes
TW-TNN|福泰飯桌第三代.text: The third generation of an 80-plus-year-old fan zhuo zai, a classic Tainan eatery where you pick from the dishes on display. What's on offer depends on what came in that day; try the minced pork rice with something like braised napa cabbage.

TW-TNN|西羅殿牛肉湯.dish: Beef-bone broth with thinly sliced beef
TW-TNN|西羅殿牛肉湯.text: A beef soup shop that opens at 4:30 a.m. Broth made from beef bones, brisket and onion comes with thinly sliced beef. Order a soup and you get minced pork rice too. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

TW-TNN|葉家小卷米粉.dish: Baby squid and thick rice noodle soup
TW-TNN|葉家小卷米粉.text: A shop on Guohua Street run by three generations since 1935. Thick noodles made from brown rice come in a sweet squid broth. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays, and it shuts soon after lunch, so go early.

TW-TNN|江水號.dish: Shaved ice with your choice of toppings (ba bao bing)
TW-TNN|江水號.text: A shaved ice shop that started in West Market in 1931 and is now run by the third generation. Choose freely from over a dozen toppings, including taro paste, rice balls and beans. In winter there's also a sweet sticky-rice porridge with rice wine.

TW-KHH|前金肉燥飯.dish: Minced pork-fat rice with fish floss
TW-KHH|前金肉燥飯.text: Open since 1959 and now run by the third generation. The minced topping, made from back fat, isn't greasy and melts in your mouth. The classic way is with fish floss and a soft-boiled duck egg. When it's sold out, they close.

TW-KHH|菜粽李.dish: Sticky rice dumplings with peanuts only (cai zong)
TW-KHH|菜粽李.text: A rice dumpling shop run by three generations, filled with nothing but sticky rice and peanuts. Wrapped by hand every day, they're served with sauce and peanut powder alongside a bowl of miso soup. Opens at 6:30 a.m.

TW-KHH|李家圓仔湯.text: At the entrance to Yancheng First Public Market since 1953. The signature is a simple shaved ice topped with red beans, mung beans, taro and handmade rice balls. On the winter solstice and at the Lantern Festival, locals come for rice balls.

TW-KHH|阿忠米粉湯.dish: Thick rice noodle soup with milkfish or baby squid
TW-KHH|阿忠米粉湯.text: A breakfast spot with no sign, now run by the third generation. It began with milkfish and thick rice noodle soup, and the version with boiled baby squid has become a signature too. Locals also order fried squid or fish skin.

TW-PIF|福記餛飩.text: A wonton shop deep in an alley near Pingtung Night Market, said to have been run by four generations for a century. The noodles in sesame-peanut sauce come with dried radish for a nice crunch.

TW-PIF|正老牌潮州冷熱冰.dish: Hot-and-cold shaved ice (leng re bing) over warm rice balls and beans
TW-PIF|正老牌潮州冷熱冰.text: Warm peanut-filled rice balls, taro and red beans on the bottom; shaved ice and brown sugar syrup on top. This Chaozhou specialty is all about scooping up hot and cold together, and the shop recommends not stirring it.

TW-PIF|葉家肉粿.dish: Steamed rice cake in rich fish-bone broth (rou gui)
TW-PIF|葉家肉粿.text: A shop run by three generations, where Donggang locals pick up breakfast. A steamed rice cake is topped with sausage, sakura shrimp and pork, doused in a rich fish-bone broth and eaten with garlic sauce.

TW-HUA|液香扁食.text: Going for about 70 years, with just one thing on the menu: wonton soup, ten wontons to a bowl. It's open only four hours, from 9:30 a.m. to just after lunch, and closed on Sundays.

TW-HUA|廟口紅茶.dish: Iced black tea from steel pipes, with small pastries
TW-HUA|廟口紅茶.text: Three steel pipes inside the shop dispense black tea, almond tea and plum juice. It opens at 6 a.m., and pairing a drink with the little baked pastries is the old-school way locals love.

TW-HUA|中一豆花.dish: Douhua (silken tofu pudding) with tapioca pearls or peanuts
TW-HUA|中一豆花.text: A douhua shop near the seaside park in Meilun, going for more than 40 years. The two basic flavors are tapioca and peanut, at about NT$40 a bowl. Open 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.

TW-TTT|老東台米苔目.dish: Thick rice noodles (mi tai mu) with minced pork
TW-TTT|老東台米苔目.text: Started in 1955 as a stall beside a movie theater and now run by third-generation brothers. Thick rice noodles are topped with minced pork, and you can have them in soup or dry.

TW-TTT|卑南豬血湯.dish: Pork blood cake and intestine soup in bone broth
TW-TTT|卑南豬血湯.text: Over 60 years since it began as a pushcart, now run by the third generation. Thick slices of pork blood cake and intestine simmered in bone broth, with a small plate of dressed vegetables on the side: an old Taitung breakfast.

TW-TTT|寶桑豆花.dish: Douhua (silken tofu pudding) with peanuts or mung beans
TW-TTT|寶桑豆花.text: Started on Baosang Road in 1979 and moved to its current spot on Zhengqi Road in 2010. Douhua made fresh daily is topped with peanuts or mung beans cooked until meltingly soft. Warm douhua is available in winter.

TW-PEN|北新橋牛雜湯.dish: Beef offal soup with tripe and tongue in beef-bone broth
TW-PEN|北新橋牛雜湯.text: A breakfast-only shop going for more than 50 years, closing before noon. Beef bones simmer for six hours to make the broth, which comes with tripe and tongue. Locals add a meat bun or chive bun for breakfast.

TW-PEN|鐘記燒餅.dish: Clay-oven flatbread (shao bing) filled with a scallop and scallion omelet
TW-PEN|鐘記燒餅.text: On Wenkang Street, lined with breakfast shops, for more than 40 years and now run by the second generation. The flatbread, baked in a clay-jar oven, is crisp outside and chewy inside. The favorite filling is a scallion omelet with a fried dough stick.

TW-PEN|旭西餅舖.dish: Zha zao, round fried sweets for celebrations
TW-PEN|旭西餅舖.text: A Huxi pastry shop going for over half a century. Zha zao are fried sweets you can't do without at weddings, temple festivals and other celebrations, and many of those sold in Magong come from here. They sell out in the morning.

TW-KIN|標記小吃店.dish: Handmade egg crepes (dan bing) and Cantonese congee
TW-KIN|標記小吃店.text: A breakfast shop near East Gate Market, going for more than 55 years. The signature dan bing is made from scratch, dough and all, and there's also Cantonese congee, vermicelli and Kinmen fried dough sticks. An everyday breakfast for Kinmen locals.

TW-KIN|蚵嗲之家.text: A fritter shop in Jincheng going for more than 40 years. Besides fritters made with Kinmen's own rock oysters, there are spring rolls and sesame balls. It's open only a few hours, from 2:30 p.m. until early evening.

TW-KIN|談天樓.dish: Shaved ice with black-sesame rice balls (tang yuan bing)
TW-KIN|談天樓.text: A dessert shop in Shanwai since 1954. The famous tang yuan bing puts hot, hand-rolled sesame rice balls on cold shaved ice, and young soldiers doing military service used to come here when they missed home. There are beef noodles tossed in sauce too.

TW-LIE|阿妹的店.dish: Ding bian hu, a Fuzhou-style breakfast soup with thin rice batter
TW-LIE|阿妹的店.text: On the second floor of Shizi Market, which only opens in the mornings, and a regular breakfast stop for locals. It opens at 5:30 a.m. and can sell out by around 8, so get up early. Pair it with a jiguang bun from the same market.

TW-LIE|萬家香二店.dish: Gou mian, hand-rolled noodles, with wonton soup
TW-LIE|萬家香二店.text: In Chinese, gou mian reads like “dog noodles,” but no dogs are involved: the name comes from a Fuzhou word for noodles rolled out with a stick. Local guides say this place is a must, and the combo of noodles plus wonton soup is a favorite.

hot.tip: Hot and humid: a short walk is enough to get you sweating. Indoor air-conditioning is strong, so always carry a light layer. Bring a hat or parasol, and drink water often.

warm.tip: The most comfortable temperature, though humidity runs high. Afternoon thunderstorms can roll in, so pack a folding umbrella.

mild.tip: Easy walking weather by day, cool only in the mornings and evenings. A light jacket or an extra shirt is just right.

cool.tip: In the north, this temperature comes with a damp chill that feels colder than the number suggests. A windproof jacket works better than a thick sweater.

chilly.tip: Many buildings in Taiwan have no heating, so it's often just as cold indoors. Dress in layers, and adding a scarf makes a real difference.

cold.tip: Rare in the lowlands: expect this during a cold snap or up in the mountains (Alishan, Hehuanshan, Taipingshan). You'll need serious cold-weather gear and a windproof, waterproof jacket.

info.gist: Visa-free? You still need to file an arrival card online
rows: Many nationalities can enter without a visa, for 90, 30 or 14 days depending on your passport. The official list from the Bureau of Consular Affairs (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) is the final word, so check the rules for your nationality there.
If you enter visa-free, you must submit the Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC) online. Paper cards are no longer handed out. Do it before you leave and you'll get through faster on arrival.

info.gist: High-speed rail, Taiwan Railway, metro and tourist buses
rows: Links Taipei and Zuoying (Kaohsiung) in about 1 hr 35 min–2 hr 15 min, covering the major cities of the west coast.
A rail network that circles the island. The best way to travel the east (Yilan, Hualien, Taitung) and the scenic branch lines (Pingxi, Jiji and Neiwan).
Runs in Taipei, Taoyuan Airport, Taichung and Kaohsiung. EasyCard works on every line.
Sightseeing bus routes linking major attractions. A big help if you're traveling without a car.
Bike sharing. Register your EasyCard and a phone number to start riding.

info.gist: One card for the metro, buses and convenience stores
rows: A stored-value card for the MRT, buses, Taiwan Railway and convenience stores. Buy and top it up at convenience stores.
The currency is the New Taiwan dollar (TWD). Night markets and small eateries mostly take cash, so keep small change handy.
Change money at the airport or at banks in town. Convenience store ATMs widely accept foreign cards for cash withdrawals.
There's no tipping culture, though some restaurants add a 10% service charge.

info.gist: Buying an eSIM before you leave is quickest
rows: Tourist SIMs and eSIMs are sold at Taoyuan, Songshan and Kaohsiung airports. Unlimited data plans are the norm.
Free Wi-Fi (such as iTaiwan) is common at stations, convenience stores and on the MRT.

info.gist: October and November are the easiest months to travel
rows: March to May is a pleasant spring. June to September is hot and humid, and it's typhoon season. October and November are the best months to travel. From December to February, the north is damp and chilly while the south stays mild.
Mornings and evenings get cold in the mountains (Alishan, Taipingshan, Hehuanshan), so bring warm layers.

info.gist: Need help? Call the multilingual hotline
rows: Police 110 / Fire and ambulance 119. Tourist information hotline 0800-011-765 (24 hours, in Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean).
No eating or drinking on the MRT, not even water or gum.
110 V, with Type A plugs (two flat pins). If your plugs are different, bring an adapter, and check that your devices work on 110 V.

steps: Take a TR local or Tze-Chiang train from Taipei to Keelung
Take the Airport MRT express to Taipei Main Station (about 35 min, NT$160)
Change to TR for Keelung (about 40–55 min)

TW-KEE.local: Heping Island, Zhengbin Fishing Port and Lover's Lake can be reached by city bus or taxi from Keelung Station. For the National Museum of Marine Science and Technology, take the TR Shen'ao Line to Haikeguan Station (about 10 min from Ruifang).
TW-KEE.tip: Shen'ao Line trains to Haikeguan are infrequent, so check the timetable before you set off.

steps: Take the Airport MRT from Airport Terminal 1 or Terminal 2 Station to Taipei Main Station
Express trains take about 35 min; commuter trains, which stop at every station, about 50 min
Board the MRT Wenhu Line at Songshan Airport Station
Change lines for Taipei Main Station

TW-TPE.local: The MRT is the best way around the city. For Taipei 101, ride the Tamsui-Xinyi Line to Taipei 101/World Trade Center Station (about 15 min from Taipei Main Station). The Xinbeitou hot springs are right by Xinbeitou Station, and Yangmingshan is about 35 min from Beitou Station on the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Beitou-Zhuzihu Route. For the National Palace Museum, buses such as R30 leave from Exit 1 of Shilin Station (about 15 min).
TW-TPE.pass: Taiwan PASS, sold to foreign visitors, bundles a 3-day THSR or TR pass with the MRT and other transport (THSR version NT$2,800, TR version NT$2,500).
TW-TPE.tip: Bus R30 from Exit 1 of Shilin Station is the handiest way to the National Palace Museum, and it drops you at B1 of the main building.

Take TR from Taipei to Ruifang (about 35–55 min)
Change to the Pingxi Line for Shifen (about 30 min)
Take the MRT Tamsui-Xinyi Line from Taipei Main Station to Tamsui

TW-NWT.local: Shifen and Pingxi are also served by the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Muzha-Pingxi Route from MRT Taipei Zoo Station: about 50 min to Pingxi Old Street and 70 min to Shifen. For Yehliu and the Juming Museum, take the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Crown North Coast Route from Tamsui Station (about 1 hr 40 min to Yehliu). Fulong is 1–2 hours from Taipei Main Station by TR.
TW-NWT.tip: From November to April, the Crown North Coast Route runs only on weekends and public holidays. On weekdays, use New Taipei city buses such as the 862 and 863 to get along the North Coast.

From Bus Stop 9, ride the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Daxi Express to Daxi Old Street (about 40 min)
Take the Airport MRT to THSR Taoyuan Station (about 20 min)
Ride the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Daxi Express to Daxi Old Street (about 40 min)

TW-TAO.local: Daxi Old Street and Cihu are both on the Daxi Express route, with Cihu about 50 min from THSR Taoyuan Station. Xiao Wulai and Dongyanshan each have their own Taiwan Tourist Shuttle route.
TW-TAO.tip: The Xiao Wulai Route runs only on weekends and public holidays.

Take THSR from Taipei to Hsinchu (about 30–35 min)
Walk through the 2nd-floor concourse to TR Liujia Station and ride the Liujia Line to Hsinchu Station (about 20 min)

TW-HSZ.local: The sights in central Hsinchu are clustered around TR Hsinchu Station. For Nanliao, Qingcao Lake and Shibajian Mountain, take a city bus or taxi.
TW-HSZ.tip: THSR Hsinchu Station is out in Zhubei, in Hsinchu County. To reach central Hsinchu City, change to the TR Liujia Line.

Take THSR from Taipei to Hsinchu (about 30–35 min)
From TR Liujia Station, change at Zhuzhong to the Neiwan Line for Neiwan

TW-HSQ.local: Beipu Old Street and Green World Ecological Farm are on the Lions Head Mountain Route (about 35–40 min from THSR Hsinchu Station). Neiwan Old Street sits at the end of the Neiwan Line, about 45 min from Zhuzhong Station.
TW-HSQ.tip: Few Neiwan Line trains run through from Hsinchu Station, so most trips involve a change at Zhuzhong.

steps: Take TR from Taipei to Luodong (about 1 hr 15 min–1 hr 40 min)
From Luodong Transfer Station, take the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Dongshan River Route to the Traditional Arts Center (about 25 min)

TW-ILA.local: For Jiaoxi Hot Springs and Wufengqi, take the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Jiaoxi Route from TR Jiaoxi Station (about 10 min to Wufengqi). Dongshan River Water Park and the National Center for Traditional Arts are 15–25 min from Luodong Transfer Station on the Dongshan River Route.
TW-ILA.tip: Local trains take over 2 hours from Taipei to Yilan. Many Tze-Chiang and Puyuma trains don't sell standing tickets, so reserve a seat in advance.

Take a TR local train from Taipei to Sanyi

TW-MIA.local: Nanzhuang Old Street is near the end of the Nanzhuang Route. The Sanyi Wood Sculpture Museum, Shengxing Station and Longteng Broken Bridge are best covered by car or taxi from Sanyi Station.
TW-MIA.tip: Only local trains run direct from Taipei to Sanyi, and the trip takes about 2.5 hours.

TR Xinwuri Station, the Taichung MRT and the bus bays are all connected to the station

TW-TXG.local: Head into the city by TR from Xinwuri, the Taichung MRT or bus. For Gaomei Wetlands, take the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Taichung Dynamic Coast Route from Dajia Station on the TR Coast Line (about 20 min). Dasyueshan is about 2 hours from Fengyuan Bus Transfer Center on the Taiwan Tourist Shuttle Dasyueshan Route.
TW-TXG.pass: Foreign visitors can buy a THSR 3-Day Pass (3 days in a row) or a Flexible 2-Day Pass (any 2 days within 7).
TW-TXG.tip: The Taichung Dynamic Coast Route runs from the Da'an Harbor area to Taichung Airport, and Gaomei Wetlands is one of the stops along the way.

TW-CHA.local: In Lukang, the old street, Tianhou Temple and Longshan Temple are all close together in the town center. The Changhua Roundhouse and Baguashan are reached from TR Changhua Station.
TW-CHA.tip: The Lukang Blessing Express runs only a few times a day, so check the return times before you go.

TW-NAN.tip: The Sun Moon Lake and Xitou routes often fill up on weekends, and you may not get on at stops along the way. Line up at the start of the route, Gancheng Bus Station in Taichung, or at THSR Taichung Station.
