TW-CYI.tip: THSR Chiayi Station is in Taibao, in Chiayi County, so you'll need a bus into the city center. Forest railway tickets go on sale online 14 days before travel.

TW-LIE.tip: Strong winds and thick fog can delay or cancel both flights and ferries, so leave some slack in your schedule.

numbers.label: Foreigners in Taiwan hotline (National Immigration Agency)
numbers.note: 24 hours. Chinese, English and Japanese every day of the year. Can also help with interpreting

steps.title: Lost passport
steps.body: Report the loss at the nearest National Immigration Agency office and get a loss report (if you have other photo ID, the police can issue one too). Then contact your country's embassy or representative office in Taiwan about a replacement passport or an emergency travel document, and ask what to bring. Requirements differ by country, so also check what you'll need to show at immigration when you leave.

steps.title: Illness or injury
steps.body: In an emergency, call 119 for an ambulance. Your embassy or representative office may be able to recommend hospitals with English-speaking staff. Contact your travel insurer as well.

steps.title: Theft or lost property
steps.body: If something is stolen, call 110 or go to the nearest police station, and ask for a copy of the report. If your passport was taken too, report it to both the National Immigration Agency and the police. If language is a problem, call 1990 for interpreting help.

steps.title: Typhoons and earthquakes
steps.body: When a typhoon is on its way, follow the Central Weather Administration forecasts and check each operator's official site for cancelled trains, ferries and flights. If an earthquake hits, protect your head, and once things settle, call the tourist information hotline at 0800-011-765 for updates.

lines: Hey, did you know only one county in Taiwan has no coastline?
This is Nantou, right in the middle of the island. Just mountains all around.
So instead of the sea, it's got a lake: Sun Moon Lake.
In winter, the maples at Aowanda turn bright red,
and Cingjing Farm is a ranch above a sea of clouds, apparently.
Sigh, lucky you. I've only ever seen it in model form.
The director never takes me anywhere.
So go for me, okay? Next time you're in Taiwan, head for the middle.
This has been RINKA from MV STUDIO.
Oh, and don't tell the director I said that, okay?

TW-TPE: Hey, see how Taipei looks like a donut hole on this model?
It's New Taipei all the way around. The capital's totally boxed in.
And right in the middle of the hole, Taipei 101 just shoots up.
The National Palace Museum has almost 700,000 treasures,
and in Beitou, you can literally take the metro to a hot spring.
The director sent me nothing but night market pics again yesterday.
So if it's your first time in Taiwan, start with Taipei, okay?
If something's really good, tell me. Just between us.
Oh, and not a word to the director about the night market, okay?
TW-NWT: Hey, guess which city in Taiwan has the most people. Hint: not Taipei.
The big ring that wraps all the way around Taipei.
Out by the sea, there's a rock that looks like a queen's profile.
In Shifen, people write wishes on lanterns and send them up,
and Jiufen's an old town that's all slopes and stairs.
Ah, I so want to send up a lantern. I've got a million wishes.
I asked the director, and apparently my wishes won't fit. Rude, right?
So once you're in Taipei, go explore the ring around it too.
This has been RINKA, out in New Taipei.
Oh, and my wishes? Those stay a secret from the director, okay?
TW-TAO: Hey, know where most people flying into Taiwan land first?
Taoyuan! The big airport's here, so almost everyone comes through.
But it's not just an airport town, apparently.
Daxi Old Street is lined with old brick buildings,
and around Shimen Reservoir, the thing to eat is fresh fish.
Lucky you. Your trip starts the second you walk out of the airport.
I can't even get to the gate.
The director always skips it, since it's "just a layover."
So when you land, get out of the airport and take a little detour.
This has been RINKA, from the city where your trip begins.
Oh, and don't tell the director I ratted them out, okay?
TW-TXG: Hey, know the city where you can get ice cream in an old eye clinic?
It's Taichung, a big city around the middle of Taiwan.
The building's called Miyahara. These days it's a sweets shop.
Rainbow Village started when one grandpa began painting its walls,
and bubble tea? People say it was born in Taichung.
Sigh, the home of bubble tea. And I can't even hold a straw.
The director keeps bragging about having three cups the day they went.
So start with one cup in Taichung. Tell me how the real thing tastes.
This has been RINKA, from the home of bubble tea.
Oh, and the three cups? Forget you heard that, okay?
TW-TNN: Hey, ever heard of a city where people have beef soup for breakfast?
That's Tainan. They say it's the oldest city in Taiwan.
It started about 400 years ago, when the Dutch built a fort here.
Some beef soup places open around four in the morning,
and there are temples just about everywhere you look.
Ugh, breakfast talk is cruel. I don't get hungry, but now I kinda am.
Every Tainan pic the director sends me is of half-eaten food.
So get to Tainan in the morning. Being an early bird totally pays off.
This has been RINKA in Tainan.
Oh, and don't mention the half-eaten food around the director.
TW-KHH: Hey, wanna see a harbor where old warehouses became one big art scene?
It's Kaohsiung, the big port city down in southern Taiwan.
Pier-2 is in the old harbor warehouses, and it's packed with art.
Cijin's just a quick boat ride across,
and at night, the lights reflecting on the Love River are gorgeous.
Ooh, a boat ride sounds nice. I probably wouldn't even get seasick.
The director took seasick pills before boarding. For a ride that short!
So take the boat in Kaohsiung. The breeze is supposed to be amazing.
This has been RINKA, from Kaohsiung, home of Pier-2 and the Love River.
Oh, and the seasick pills? That stays between us.
TW-KEE: Hey, did you know there's a city so rainy they call it the Rain Port?
It's Keelung, a harbor town up north, a train ride from Taipei.
Miaokou Night Market sits right in front of a temple.
It's packed with food stalls and super lively,
and Heping Island has rocks the waves carved into wild shapes.
Lucky you. A rainy night market. I've never even held an umbrella.
The director's Keelung pics always have raindrops on the lens.
So bring an umbrella to Keelung. You'll probably need it.
This has been RINKA, from rainy Keelung.
Oh, and don't tell the director about the raindrop pics, okay?
TW-HSZ: Hey, guess which place is so windy they call it the Windy City?
It's Hsinchu City. In fall and winter, the wind really howls.
Rice noodles get dried in that wind, which supposedly makes them great.
By the City God Temple, you can get rice noodles and pork ball soup,
and the world's biggest contract chipmaker has its headquarters here.
Sigh, I'd love to feel the wind. I've never even felt a breeze.
The director's hat blew off twice. Kinda wish I'd seen that.
So if you're going to Hsinchu City, hang on to your hat.
This has been RINKA, from the Windy City.
Oh, and the flying hat? Pretend you never saw it.
TW-HSQ: Hey, know about the old railway town at a tiny mountain station?
This is Hsinchu County, the mountainous one next to Hsinchu City.
That town's called Neiwan, and it's got an old Hakka street.
You can ride the Neiwan Line train out there, nice and slow,
and with Hakka lei cha, you grind tea leaves and beans in a bowl.
All that grinding looks so fun. I can't even touch the bowl.
The director ground so much their arm hurt, and complained nonstop.
So in Hsinchu County, grind your own lei cha, okay?
This has been RINKA, from Neiwan, the old railway town.
Oh, and no laughing about the sore arm in front of the director, okay?
TW-MIA: Hey, heard of a mountain where white flowers fall like snow in May?
It's Miaoli. Hills, mountains, and lots of Hakka people.
Those white flowers are tung blossoms. People call them May snow.
Dahu grows more strawberries than anywhere else in Taiwan,
and Hakka floral fabric is covered in big, bold flower prints.
Strawberry picking, so jealous. I can't even sneak a bite.
The director ate about half of them while picking.
So in Miaoli, pick a whole basket of strawberries, okay?
This has been RINKA, from the land of strawberries and Hakka florals.
Oh, and the snacking? Keep it quiet, as a favor to the director.
TW-CHA: Hey, ever seen a train shed that opens out like a folding fan?
It's Changhua, out west. Rice paddies and old towns.
That's the Changhua Roundhouse. Locomotives still come and go there.
Lukang still has old streets from its days as a port town,
and on Baguashan, a giant Buddha looks out over the city.
Sigh, I wish I could see a train spin around. I only know model ones.
The director keeps sending pics in the same pose by the locomotives.
So in Changhua, go see the turntable in the middle of the roundhouse.
This has been RINKA, from the town with the fan-shaped roundhouse.
Oh, and if you mention the same-pose thing, the director will sulk.
TW-YUN: Hey, know the county where a hand puppet show became a huge TV hit?
It's Yunlin, one of Taiwan's biggest farming counties.
The show is budaixi glove puppetry, and Yunlin is crazy about it.
Beigang Chaotian Temple is famous for the goddess Mazu,
and Yunlin grows more peanuts than anywhere else in Taiwan.
I'd love to try working a puppet. Usually I'm the puppet!
The director even started doing voices for the puppets. Uninvited.
So in Yunlin, catch a budaixi show at least once.
This has been RINKA, from the home of glove puppetry.
Oh, and the voices thing? Don't say you heard it from me, okay?
TW-CYI: Hey, know which city is famous for chicken rice?
It's Chiayi City, a cozy little city in western Taiwan.
Here's the thing: Chiayi's chicken rice is actually made with turkey.
Hinoki Village is lined with old cypress-wood houses,
and the Alishan Forest Railway runs from this city up the mountain.
Turkey rice, so jealous. I can't even smell it.
The director hit three places in a single day.
So in Chiayi City, try a few turkey rice spots and compare.
This has been RINKA, from the home of turkey "chicken rice."
Oh, and the food crawl? Don't mention it around the director.
TW-CYQ: Hey, know where people get up at night for sunrise above the clouds?
That's Alishan, and it's right here in Chiayi County.
Sunrise chasers take a super early train up to the lookout.
Up top, there are a bunch of huge sacred trees,
and Alishan tea grows way up high, so it smells amazing.
Sigh, I wish I could try getting up early. Not that I ever sleep.
The director overslept and missed the sunrise train.
So the night before Alishan, get to bed early, okay?
This has been RINKA, from Chiayi County, home of Alishan.
Oh, and the oversleeping? Let's keep that between the two of us.
TW-PIF: Hey, what do you think the very southern tip of Taiwan is like?
It's Pingtung. Kenting's here too, down on the southern coast.
The climate's tropical, so it feels like a whole other country.
Tons of tropical fruit grows here, like mangoes and wax apples,
and from the very southern tip, you can see three seas at once.
A warm sea? Not fair. I can't even touch water.
The director came back so tan, they looked like a different person.
So when you go to Pingtung, don't forget sunscreen.
This has been RINKA, from the southern end of Taiwan.
Oh, and please don't ask the director about the tan, okay?
TW-ILA: Hey, ever seen an island out at sea shaped like a turtle?
It's Yilan, on the far side of a long mountain tunnel from Taipei.
It's Guishan Island, and it really does look like a swimming turtle.
Jiaoxi is a whole hot spring town,
and Sanxing scallions are so good they've become famous.
Ah, I'd love a long soak in a hot bath. I wouldn't even overheat.
The director planned on a quick foot bath and vanished for two hours.
So in Yilan, take your time and really soak in the hot springs.
This has been RINKA, from a town full of hot spring steam.
Oh, and don't tell anyone I leaked the two-hour thing, okay?
TW-HUA: Hey, notice how the right side of this model is almost all mountains?
Hualien. Biggest county in Taiwan, about an eighth of the island.
And by the sea, there's a beach lined with round stones, not sand.
At night, there's a big night market where the old station used to be,
and up in the gorge, they're still slowly fixing the roads.
Hmm, I'd have loved to walk that beach barefoot. Not that I have feet.
The director sent me thirty pics of rocks. They all look the same!
So take your time in Hualien. It's huge, so don't rush it.
This has been RINKA, your Hualien guide.
Oh, and the rock pics? Keep that from the director, okay?
TW-TTT: Hey, know where hot-air balloons fill the sky on summer mornings?
It's Taitung, on Taiwan's east coast, facing the Pacific.
That highland is called Luye Highland,
and every summer, there's a hot-air balloon festival.
In Chishang, you can bike Mr. Brown Avenue through the rice paddies,
and Zhiben is Taitung's most famous hot spring town.
Hot-air balloons, so jealous. I think I'd be fine with heights.
The director got on and spent the whole ride not looking down.
So ride a balloon in Taitung, okay? Tell me what the view's like.
This has been RINKA, under Taitung's balloon-filled sky.
Oh, and the not-looking-down thing? Don't let the director find out.
TW-PEN: Hey, did you know tons of islands sit between Taiwan and the mainland?
It's Penghu, a county made up of about ninety islands.
Old lava hardened into cliffs of rock columns, all standing in rows.
From spring into summer, there are fireworks shows over the sea,
and the heart-shaped stone weirs were built long ago to catch fish.
Wow, I'd love to see those heart-shaped weirs.
I've never even seen the tide go out.
The director tried to shoot the heart from a boat. Never got the angle.
So before Penghu, look up a spot where you can see it from above.
This has been RINKA, from Penghu and its ninety islands.
Oh, and the bad-angle story? Only when the director's not around.
TW-KIN: Hey, guess which Taiwan island looks right across at a mainland city?
It's Kinmen. It's way closer to the mainland than to Taiwan proper.
The villages still have lots of old houses with red tile roofs.
At village entrances, Wind Lion Gods stand guard against the wind,
and the famous cleavers here are made from old artillery shells.
Sigh, every Wind Lion God has its own face, and I can't go meet them.
The director posed for a photo making the exact same face as one.
So in Kinmen, go find your favorite Wind Lion God.
This has been RINKA, from Kinmen, land of red tiles and Wind Lion Gods.
Oh, and don't show the director that same-face photo, okay?
TW-LIE: Hey, did you know there's an island where the sea glows blue at night?
It's Matsu. Officially, the county's called Lienchiang.
That glow comes from tiny sea creatures. They call it the blue tears.
Qinbi's stone houses up the hillside are said to look Mediterranean,
and the glowing sea shows up best on dark nights, spring to summer.
Sigh, a glowing sea. I mean, I glow too, just on a screen.
The director waited three days and didn't see it once.
So when you go to Matsu, give yourself a few extra days.
This has been RINKA, from Matsu, where the sea glows at night.
Oh, and the three-day wait? Let's not bring it up around the director.
